A drive is recognised wherever it is mounted, and a different drive (or an empty mount point) at the same path is reported as wrong drive and never written to. civex never creates a missing volume folder outside the project, because an unmounted drive's path would otherwise be recreated on the wrong disk.

Network drives work when your OS has mounted them (an NFS or SMB share under /mnt or /Volumes, a mapped drive letter, a UNC path). civex doesn't mount shares or hold credentials. A share that stops answering is reported offline within a few seconds, and work on other volumes carries on.

Adding a volume checks it first: whether the folder exists or will be made, is writable, has room, is a separate disk from the project, or already belongs to another volume. The app's Add drive form shows the same checks as you type.

docs.title: Files in a bucket instead
docs.text:
A project can keep its files in an S3 bucket (or anything that speaks S3's API: MinIO, Cloudflare R2) instead of on drives. Choose it under Settings → Storage → Tasks → Use a bucket…, or from the command line:

export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=… AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=…
civex store bucket check lab-files --endpoint http://127.0.0.1:9000   # try it
civex store bucket set lab-files --prefix projects/survey-2024          # use it
civex store bucket show --check
civex store bucket clear                                              # drives again

Either way civex tries the bucket first: it must be reachable, accept a write, read it back and delete it, and hold nothing under the prefix already (another project's files there would look unused to a clean-up here). Files are never moved between drives and a bucket, so a project can switch only while the place it leaves holds none of its files: start a project in a bucket, or switch before adding files. civex doctor warns if files are still recorded on drives while a bucket is in use. The settings are saved in _civex/config.toml:

[store.s3]
bucket = "lab-files"
prefix = "projects/survey-2024"     # optional: a folder inside the bucket
region = "eu-west-2"              # optional
endpoint = "http://minio:9000"    # for MinIO and the like
profile = "lab"                   # an AWS profile; else the default chain

Credentials are never in config.toml: boto3 reads them from the environment (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID…), the named profile, or the machine's role. Objects are laid out as on a drive (<prefix>/3f/9c01ab…), the same inventory records what is there, and records, history, sync and clean-up work unchanged. The bucket is one volume that is always online, so the drive pages and commands don't apply to such a project: Settings → Storage shows the bucket instead.

Files go straight to the bucket. Unless direct = false, downloads from the app are a redirect to the bucket, and a device syncing with an authority whose files are in a bucket sends and receives them by presigned URL, so the bytes never pass through civex. A file sent in parts is checked against its hash by a read-back during the next clean-up, and one that doesn't match is removed. Uploads from the browser still go through the server, which hashes them before putting them in the bucket.

docs.title: Where new files go
docs.text:
1. The collection's home volume, if it has one and the home can take the file.
  2. Otherwise the write queue, in order, skipping volumes that can't take it.
civex store place set survey-2024 archive                       # home
civex store place set survey-2024 archive --on-unavailable fail # never anywhere else
civex store place list
civex store place clear survey-2024

Homes are keyed by collection id in config.toml ([store.placement.<id>]), so renaming a collection changes nothing. Setting or clearing a home moves no existing files.

Content already on any drive is reused, not written again. The one exception: a collection's home gets its own copy of content it doesn't hold yet.

docs.title: Copies and what records point at
docs.text:
The same content can be on several drives. Each record's file points at exactly one copy. That makes "where are this collection's files" a fact, not a guess:

  • civex store collections and Settings → Storage count each collection on the copies its live records point at.
  • A copy that records from several collections point at is counted once, under Shared by several collections, so a drive's rows add up to what it holds.
  • civex store where <record> lists a record's files and the drive each is on; --details adds paths on disk and what else uses each file.

Where a file is stored belongs to this computer. It isn't part of the record and doesn't sync.

docs.title: Moving files
docs.text:
Move CLI What moves Empty a drive civex store move --off old --to archive Everything on old Gather a collection civex store move --collection survey-2024 --to archive What its live records point at Gather a selection civex files gather --in survey-2024 --on field-ssd --to archive Just those files

All three work the same way:

  • A move repoints. The records it covers point at the target. A file is copied there unless the target already has that content, in which case nothing is copied. The old copy is removed once nothing points at it. If records the move doesn't cover still use it, it stays (copied, not moved). The preview says how many files are copied, how many are already there, and what space is freed.
  • It can't lose files. Each file is copied to a scratch file, checked against its hash, renamed into place, recorded, and then removed from the source. Stopping at any point leaves each file in its old place, its new place, or both.
  • One at a time. A second move waits its turn (civex store transfers list). Ctrl+C in the terminal pauses. civex store transfers resume <id> carries on, and pause/cancel work from another terminal or the app.
  • A drive being emptied is made read-only until the move stops (finished, paused, cancelled or failed), so new files don't land on it.
  • Problems don't stop the rest. A damaged or missing file is listed and left. A full target moves on to the next --to and pauses when there is none. A drive that stops answering pauses the move, and a move started in the app resumes by itself when the drive is back.

docs.title: Cleaning up
docs.text:
civex store gc removes copies nothing points at. It is a dry run without --apply.

civex store gc

Scanned 2 object(s) in the store.
  2 referenced by a live record or job
  0 unreferenced but within the 14-day grace period
  Collectible 0 object(s), 0 B

Kept: anything a record uses (including deleted records you can still restore), anything a workflow run uses, and anything newer than --grace-days (14). Not kept: files only old history mentions, so an old Activity entry may name a file that's gone. --volume limits it to one drive. It can't run during a move.

docs.title: In the app
docs.text:
Settings → Storage has three tabs, and above them a list of anything needing attention (an unplugged drive holding files, low space, an interrupted move).

Tab For Drives Each drive's status and space. A drive's name opens its own page: which collections are on it, unused files, moves involving it Collections Each collection's files by drive, its home, Gather, and what this computer keeps when syncing Tasks Move files…, Clean up…, and the list of moves

On records, a file on a drive that can't be reached is always marked, and its chip says which drive to plug in. With more than one volume, every file shows a chip with its drive. Settings → Advanced → Show advanced options adds full details: every copy, its path on disk, its hash, and what else uses it.

docs.title: Syncing between machines
docs.text:
One civex, the authority, holds a project's shared copy. Every other copy, a device, sends its changes there and receives everyone else's. Devices never talk to each other, and everything works offline: changes are recorded locally and go when the authority can be reached.

To set it up, follow Sync a project between computers. This page is how it behaves.

docs.title: Connecting
docs.text:
# on the authority
civex sync authority enable
civex sync device invite laptop
civex serve --sync-only            # behind HTTPS

# on a device
civex clone https://lab-pc.tail1234.ts.net my-project --invite civex_inv_…
civex sync connect https://… --invite civex_inv_…   # an existing project
This project The authority Connecting… Empty Has data makes this a copy of it Has data Empty fills the authority Has data Has data is refused: two projects can't be merged The same project picks up where it left off
  • Invites work once, for 24 hours (--hours), and are shown once. They start with civex_inv_, so secret scanners catch one pasted by mistake.
  • Or ask to join. Connect without an invite and the device shows a code (ABCD-2345) and waits. On the authority, civex sync device approve ABCD-2345 laptop (or Settings → Sync → Asking to join) lets it in by name, civex sync device deny turns it away, and a code nobody approves in 15 minutes lapses. The device is then a device like any invited one. When the server has a page for it (the hub does), the device shows that address with the code instead: open it and enter the code. civex clone <address> does the same without --invite, and civex auth status shows this device's name, id, whether it has joined, and the last sync error.
  • Keys: joining makes the device a key pair. It then signs in with its key for short sessions, and checks the authority's key, so a different server at the same address gets nothing. civex sync device revoke <name> stops a device at once. Revoking stops the device syncing; it does not wipe what it already copied: those records and files stay on that computer (the same holds when a person's access is narrowed, below).
  • HTTPS or SSH only. Devices refuse http:// except to this computer. Use Tailscale, or bind civex serve --sync-only to 127.0.0.1 behind a reverse proxy (Caddy, nginx). --sync-only serves only /api/sync/v1/. Never put the full app on a network: it has no sign-in. On a machine you can SSH into, an ssh:// address needs no server running at all (Over SSH instead).
  • A server or a device, not both. A project that serves devices can't connect to another server, and one that follows a server can't serve devices: civex refuses either. To make the old server follow a new one (moving servers), stop it serving first (Settings → Sync, or civex sync authority disable) and connect its devices to the new one. A project set up both ways by hand doesn't sync until one is turned off, and says so.
  • Big projects show progress while copying, and an interrupted copy finishes when you connect again. Records arrive first. History and files follow in the background.

docs.title: When it syncs
docs.text:
While civex serve runs, a few seconds after each change and every minute. Without the app, civex sync watch does the same in a terminal.

To… CLI App (Settings → Sync) Sync now civex sync now Sync now (also in the status bar) See where it stands civex sync status the page itself Change how often civex sync interval 300 interval Only when asked civex sync interval never Never Pause / resume civex sync pause / resume Pause / Resume Stop following civex sync disconnect Disconnect (keeps the data)

An unreachable authority is retried with back-off (up to 15 minutes). A refusal that waiting can't fix, such as a revoked device, says so and waits for you.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
Changes and files travel separately. A sync moves records only, so it takes seconds however large the files are, and a missing file never holds up a change. Files move in the background, on their own, beside syncing.

  • Sending: a device uploads files its records use that the authority lacks, with their own progress in the status bar: how many files and how much in all (120 MB of 2.1 GB), how fast, and how long is left, on one bar from the first file to the last. A file on an unplugged drive is sent once it can be read. Until the server has a file, its chip says not on the server yet (other computers can't open it), and the status bar counts such files and says why they haven't gone: going up in the background, on a drive that can't be read, or not on this computer at all (a computer that has them must send them). Send now (civex sync send from the command line) sends at once; civex sync now syncs records only and says how many files are still to go. civex remembers which files the server has said it holds and asks only about the rest; every few minutes, on Send now and on every manual sync it asks about all of them again.
  • Receiving: a file another device added arrives in the background (for collections this computer keeps), when you open it, or before an export. Until then it is marked on the server.
  • Straight to storage: an authority whose files are in a bucket (see Storage volumes) offers direct_files: a device asks it where to put a file and sends the bytes to the bucket itself, then tells the authority it is done; downloads are a redirect to the bucket. The authority only says where and records what arrived. An older device, or an authority with its files on drives, streams them as before.
  • Packs and parts: small files go many to a request (file_packs; not where files go straight to a bucket, about 32 MiB or 100 files, four requests at a time, answered per file), and a big file goes in 16 MiB parts four at a time (S3 multipart in a bucket, else file_parts on an authority with files on drives, resumable per part). Both are offered through hello; an authority without them is sent one file per request.

docs.title: Which files a computer keeps
docs.text:
Each collection either keeps its files here (downloaded in the background) or fetches them when opened. The project has a default and each collection can override it.

civex sync files                       # per collection: here, not here, setting
civex sync files opened                # default for the project (or: all)
civex sync keep survey-2024              # keep this one here
civex sync keep archive-2019 --opened  # or --reset to follow the default
civex sync free archive-2019           # remove local copies
civex sync fetch                       # download everything kept, now

Collection   Keeps                 On this computer  Not on this computer
survey-2024   every file (default)           0 (0 B)                     2

Free up space removes only copies the server confirms it holds, never one a kept collection also uses, counts first, and then sets the collection to fetch when opened so the files don't come straight back. In the app: Settings → Storage → Collections.

docs.title: Conflicts
docs.text:
What happened Result Two edits to different fields of a record Both go in Two edits to the same field The authority's value stays; yours waits on your device for review An edit to a record someone deleted The record is kept, with an item to review A delete of a record someone added something beneath The record is kept A change the authority refuses Kept on your device with the reason Two schema changes Applied in the order the authority receives them

Nothing is lost: a value that didn't go in stays on the device that made it until someone decides.

Reviewing in the app. The status bar says when something waits. Review lists it, and each record's Resolve tab settles it:

  • A clash shows the authority's value on the left and yours on the right, differences marked. Accept theirs, Accept yours, or edit the middle.
  • A refused record shows the reason and the field it names, editable in place. Fix it and save to send it again, Send unchanged, or Let it go.
  • An edit that met a delete offers Keep it or Delete it.

Keep theirs for all on the review page settles everything the authority's way, after counting, with Undo. In Activity, a change that didn't go in as made is badged Clashed, Refused, Met a delete or Not taken.

In a terminal:

civex sync conflicts [--record <id>]
civex sync resolve <conflict id> --take theirs|mine|delete|retry
civex sync resolve <conflict id> --take value --value '"M"'
civex sync resolve --all --take theirs [--kind rejected|conflict|edit_vs_delete|unfit]
civex sync reopen <conflict id>...       # take back a "theirs"

--force puts your value back even if it changed again since.

docs.title: What the authority enforces
docs.text:
A change from a device must pass the same rules as an edit on the authority: field rules (choices, limits, required, unique keys, references), where the record sits (its collection lists its schema; its parent, collection and schema aren't deleted), and schema rules (templates and unique keys name real fields).

An action travels whole. Deleting a record takes what's beneath it, and a schema change can touch several fields. If it can't go in whole, none of it does, and the device is sent back the authority's state, marked not taken.

docs.title: Who may change what
docs.text: A project in a folder is yours: everything is allowed. A hosted civex knows who is signed in and what they may do (GET /api/me: read, write records, change the structure, add or delete files, notes, shared views, delete, manage members and devices, each everywhere or in named collections), and holds a person's device to the same rule as their browser: a change a device pushes that its person may not make is refused like any change that breaks a rule, and the app shows the control switched off, saying why.

docs.title: A device that may not read everything
docs.text:
Changing the project's structure (kinds of record, their fields, collections) reaches the records of every collection, so it is for someone who can read them all: change_structure is unavailable (in Permissions itself, so for every route, service and push alike) when read is limited to some collections. Deleting a field takes delete as well, since it destroys the values held in it. A push that does either without the right is refused, and so is deleting a collection that records the device cannot see still reference. On the device itself everything stays possible locally: this is the authority's judgement on a push.

When its person may not read some collections, their device holds a partial copy: it simply never has those collections. The authority leaves them out of everything it sends that device (the feed, the copy a joining device reads, the counts it reports, and the files only they use), so no record, note, id or count of a hidden collection reaches it. A change that would put something in a collection the device may not read, or point at a record in one, is refused (the change is marked not taken, as any refused change), and so is one that names a collection it may write to for a record the authority holds in one it may not. A record moved out of sight is removed from such a device (it is never told where it went); one moved into sight is sent whole.

If the person is given more later, the device asks for it by itself: the authority says which collections the device may read (sync protocol 5), and the device reads the ones it did not have as they are now, then carries on with the feed. That includes a record that moved out of a collection it could not read into one it can, while it was away: such a record is read too (snapshot with dataset and left_after), so the feed's later changes to it apply. A device that was never told what it could read (it synced on an older protocol) reads any collection it lacks the first time it is.

A device whose person may not read everything needs protocol 5: on an older one the authority answers 426 ("update civex on this device"), because it could not be told how far the authority looked or of a collection it is given. A device whose person reads everything works on any supported protocol.

History stored by an older civex carries the collection a device claimed, not where the authority had the record. The upgrade records the feed number it happened at (sync_meta.placed_from, no rewrite of history); a limited device is sent an entry from before it only while its record is still somewhere that device may read, so a stale claim cannot carry a value out of a collection. Fetching history before joining remembers how far it looked (sync_meta.history_scan), so it can be done in steps. Values written while a record was hidden, before the upgrade, can reach a device once the record is visible again (a record carries its earlier history with it, as in hosting.md); after the upgrade the feed sends such a record only as a whole creation, and a note is placed only by changes made since the upgrade.

A hidden stretch of the feed is looked past in bounded steps: one request reads at most 2,000 entries, and when nothing in them is for the device it answers an empty page with more and through, and the device asks again from there.

If the person is given less, the authority stops sending, and that is all it can do: what the device already holds cannot be taken back. The records it copied stay on that computer, and its person can read them there. Revoking the device or removing the person is the same: it ends syncing, never the copy. A copy made again from the authority (an authority that pruned its history does this) drops what the device may no longer read. A host that needs a person never to keep data it once showed them should not give it to a device at all. Hidden collections' ids can still appear in shared things that are project-wide: the Analytics page, and the number of changes (gaps in feed numbers).

docs.title: Who a change is recorded as
docs.text: Your changes carry your OS user name, or the name set with civex sync user "Dana" (saved in the project's config.toml; --reset to undo). The authority also records which device sent each change, and Activity shows both ("Dana via laptop"). A device key proves the device, not the person.

docs.title: Sharing workflows and plugins
docs.text:
Workflows and plugins don't sync. A plugin is code, so they are shared on purpose through the authority's library: one person publishes, another installs.

civex sync library list                            # what's shared and how it stands here
civex sync library publish workflow tidy           # with the plugins it uses
civex sync library show plugin my_step -v 2        # read a version first
civex sync library install workflow tidy           # asks before writing anything
civex sync library install plugin my_step -v 1     # roll back
civex sync library remove workflow tidy -v 1
  • Nothing arrives by itself. Published text is kept in the authority's database and written into _civex/ only when someone installs it, after showing every file, its version and hash, and (for a plugin) its code.
  • The authority checks without running: safe names, 256 KB at most, valid YAML with no aliases, valid Python defining Plugin, no built-in ids.
  • Versions: each changed publish is the next version, and all are kept. A workflow pins the plugin versions it was published with. Before installing a new plugin version, civex checks every workflow here that uses it, and installs nothing that would break one unless you choose Install anyway. For a breaking change, publish a new plugin (new id) instead.
  • Who may publish: the authority's own computer always may. A device may once allowed (civex sync device allow-publish laptop), within civex sync authority library off|workflows|all (default workflows).
  • Changes that arrive by sync never start a workflow.

In the app, the Workflows page lists the library beside your own workflows with a Sharing column, and each workflow's Sharing tab has its versions.

docs.title: History
docs.text: A device whose person may read everything has the full history in Activity. A new device downloads it after joining, a little at a time. A device limited to some collections has the history of those only, and a collection it is given later is not backfilled: its earlier Activity history is not sent, only changes from then on. Edits are stored as what changed, so history stays small. Projects from civex 1.2.0 and earlier are converted in the background after opening (Tidying history in the status bar). Reclaim the space with Settings → Database → History storage or civex history compact --vacuum.

docs.title: Reliability
docs.text:
• Each change has an id, so sending one twice changes nothing.
  • The authority saves a change before answering, so a device is never told "done" for a change that wasn't saved.
  • A device finding itself ahead of an authority's history copies the project again.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text: Devices and the authority agree on the newest sync protocol both speak. When a release changes it (the changelog says "sync protocol N"), update the authority first, then the devices. A device that can't sync says which side to update.

docs.title: Moving
docs.text:
• A new authority: run civex sync connect <new address> --invite … on each device. If the old authority is to follow the new one, stop it serving first. If the new one is empty, the first device fills it. Review items about the old server are closed.
  • A device to a new computer: its id and key live in ~/.civex/sync.toml, not in the project, so a copied folder isn't the same device. Connect the copy with a new invite.

docs.title: What doesn't sync
docs.text:
Schemas, fields, collections, saved views, the Analytics page, records, the notes left on them and their files sync. These stay on each computer:

  • saved exports, and workflows and plugins (use the library);
  • config.toml settings: volumes, retention, the map, automation;
  • workflow runs and their logs;
  • pins and recent items (kept by each browser).

docs.title: Saved filters
docs.text: A saved filter keeps which records a list shows: its filter, search and sort (and the columns it was saved with). Saved filters show as chips above a list of records, so the lists a team keeps reaching for are one click away. A saved filter belongs to a kind of record, not to a person or a collection: one on sample works on samples in every collection, for everyone. (The command line and the API call them views.)

docs.title: Save one
docs.text:
Set up a list the way you want it, with + Filter or by clicking bars in the charts, then Save this filter. It keeps:

  • Filters: an AND/OR tree that may test this kind's fields, a parent's fields, or any child's ("visits that have a sample whose depth is empty").
  • Columns, in order: including parents' fields and one hop through a reference (species.common).
  • Sort: one field, ascending or descending.

Any name works except one containing /, \ or control characters (Needs review (QC) is fine).

docs.title: Use, change, remove
docs.text:
• Click a chip to apply it, and click again to drop it.
  • Change the list and the chip shows modified. Save overwrites, and Save this filter makes another.
  • The ⋮ beside an applied one renames or deletes it. Deleting a saved filter never touches records.

Saved things are marked with an icon and a word wherever they are listed (the bar above the records, pinned items, the Ctrl+K palette): a Saved filter or an Export (an export definition).

docs.title: The Analytics page
docs.text:
Analytics is one page for the whole project. Everyone sees the same page, it is in Activity, and it syncs. It holds cards: charts of records, and the built-in charts (records, storage, workflow runs, activity, AI use).

A chart gets here from a list of records: in a chart's menu, Add to Analytics page. The card keeps the chart and the records it counted (the kind, the collection, the record they were inside, the search and the filter), and draws them as they are now. Records on a card opens that list; Open shows the chart large with its numbers. For at the top narrows every chart to one collection. The filter bar applies to the built-in charts.

Anyone who may change records somewhere may press Edit page. While editing, you can drag a card or use its arrows to move it, choose Half or Full width, give it a title, take it off the page, and Add a card for a built-in chart. Done saves the page for everyone as one change; Cancel leaves it as it was. A card whose kind of record or collection is gone stays and says so until someone removes it.

civex dashboard show
civex dashboard add --schema sample --by site --measure mean:depth --in survey --size wide
civex dashboard add --schema sample --map position
civex dashboard add --widget storage --at 1
civex dashboard remove widget-storage

docs.title: Export one
docs.text:
civex view export sample "Needs review (QC)"                 # → Needs review (QC).csv
civex view export sample "Needs review (QC)" --format xlsx
civex view export sample qc --output qc.csv

Formats: csv, tsv, xlsx, json, jsonl. If the view has file columns, the output is a zip of the table plus the files, and each file cell holds the file's path inside the zip. Joined columns are named species.common, and in JSON they nest as {"species": {"common": …}}.

A view can also drive a folder export or a move: civex files export --view sample/qc, civex files gather --view sample/qc --to archive.

docs.title: Workflows
docs.text: A workflow is a YAML file in _civex/workflows/ whose steps each run a step. It runs when a record changes, or when you start it. Runs are covered in Automation.

docs.title: A complete example
docs.text:
name: read-sample-time
description: Read the sample's time from its file name.

triggers:
  record_updated:
    schema: sample
    fields: [reading]            # only when reading is set or changed

steps:
  - id: extract
    plugin: civex.value_from_filename@1
    config:
      field: reading
      pattern: '(\d{8}[-_]\d{6})'
      output_type: datetime
      date_format: 'YYYYMMDD[-_]HHmmSS'

  - id: save
    plugin: civex.set_fields@1
    config:
      field: taken_at
    inputs:
      value: extract.value       # <step id>.<output name>

Attaching 20240315_093000.csv to a sample sets its taken_at to 2024-03-15T09:30:00. Fill fields from file names walks through it.

docs.title: The file
docs.text:
Key Required Means name yes How the workflow is referred to (civex workflow run <name>) description Shown in lists enabled false switches its triggers off: it runs only when someone starts or tries it. Missing means on triggers When it runs by itself (below) record_schema Manual runs only on records of this schema inputs Plain values a manual run asks for (below). Files are asked for by a Files step steps yes id, plugin, config (the plugin's settings), inputs (other steps' outputs)

Steps run in dependency order: a step that takes extract.value runs after extract. Each plugin's settings, inputs and outputs are in the step reference, and civex plugin list shows what's installed here.

docs.title: Triggers
docs.text:
triggers:
  record_created:
    schema: sample             # every new sample
  record_updated:
    schema: sample
    fields: [reading, photo]   # only when one of these changed

Creating a record also fires record_updated for each field given a value, so a record_updated trigger on reading covers a sample created with its reading already attached. You don't need both.

Changes that arrive by sync never trigger workflows. A chain of workflows triggering each other stops after 10 hops. See Stopping automation.

docs.title: Manual runs and inputs
docs.text:
name: load-samples
record_schema: visit

steps:
  - id: readings
    plugin: civex.files@1
    config:
      source: run              # chosen each time it is run
      label: CSV files         # what the person is asked for

  - id: insert
    plugin: civex.save_records@1
    config:
      schema: sample
      if_exists: add_new
      file_field: reading
    inputs:
      files: readings.files

civex workflow list
civex workflow run load-samples --record 2d69dc46 --input "readings=readings/*.csv"

  → workflow 'load-samples' (trigger: manual)
    ✓ done
  → workflow 'read-sample-time' (trigger: record_updated)
    ✓ done

Each new sample triggered read-sample-time, so the times were filled in as well.

In the app: a record's header has Run … for the workflows that fit it. A workflow with a Files step set to be chosen when it is run asks for them first (drop files in, or, on your own computer, choose a folder: nothing is uploaded and it is faster for many files), and others start at once. To run on many records, tick them in a list and choose Run workflow on N.

docs.title: The built-in steps
docs.text:
Three groups, as the app shows them:

  • Bring in: Files (chosen when run, a folder on this computer, or a field of the record) and Table (CSV, TSV or Excel).
  • Work out: Value from the file name.
  • Save: Save as records (rows or files; update, skip or add another when a matching record exists) and Set fields on this record.

Any setting of any step may take its value from a field of the record the workflow runs on, written {from_field: name}.

docs.title: Step versions and upgrades
docs.text:
A workflow names a built-in step with its version: civex.save_records@1. A step written without one (civex.rows_to_records) is version 0: the steps civex had before steps were versioned. A step's version changes only when what a workflow can say to it changes (its settings, inputs or outputs), never for a better label or a bug fix.

When civex loads a workflow file written for older steps, it rewrites the file for the newer ones and logs what it did. The old file is kept next to it as <name>.yaml.bak (never overwritten; a second upgrade makes .bak2); backups are not workflows, and are not shared or synced. A workflow you paste, import or save is upgraded the same way. An upgrade can turn a step into different steps: civex.load_file and civex.parse_table become one Table step, inputs: {x: {type: files}} becomes a Files step named x, and the later steps are rewired. Comments in the file are not kept in the rewrite (the .bak has them). A workflow whose old steps can't be mapped (for example a step of your own reading civex.load_file's filename) is left exactly as it was, with a message saying which step to edit.

A workflow naming a step version this civex doesn't know (it came from a computer with a newer civex) is refused: "needs a newer civex". It is not run, and not touched, until civex is updated.

docs.title: Editing
docs.text:
In the app, Workflows → New workflow offers a few starting points (fill a field from a file's name, copy a field, put files on matching records, make a record for each file, run your own plugin on a file, records from a table, or nothing) and opens the builder. The builder is a form:

  • When it runs: the kind of record it runs on, and whether adding or changing one starts it (and which fields to watch).
  • Then, in order: each step's action, chosen by name ("Read a file", "Take a value from a file name"), with a sentence saying what it will do with what you chose ("Sets this record's Recorded on to the value it took from the name"), and its settings as lists of your fields and schemas. Where a step's input comes from is said in words when only one earlier step can give it, and chosen from a list when several can; Only run this step when… makes it depend on an earlier step's result.
  • A setting that is a file-name pattern has Build from an example…: pick one of the names already in that field and click the part you want (shift+ click another for several parts; tick Just the number in it for 07 out of sel07). It is found either by its place in the name ("part 2") or by the text before it ("after sel_"); the one that gives more of the names a value like yours is chosen first, and every name is shown with what it gives. For files matched to records, names that would give the same key are marked. Write the pattern yourself takes a regular expression.

YAML at the top switches to the file itself, and back: the builder changes only what it shows, so comments and anything else in the file are kept. A schema's Automations tab has New workflow for these, which starts with that schema chosen.

docs.title: Preview
docs.text:
The Preview beside the builder runs what is on screen, saved or not, on the five records of its kind changed last, and runs again a moment after each change, so you see what a change does as you make it. Choose records… picks up to ten others. For each record it says in a line what it would set or where it fails, marks the records whose result just changed, and opens to the full account: each record it would add, change or delete with the values before and after, files that matched no record, and other workflows its saves would start. Everything it did is undone each time. A workflow that asks for files when it starts shows a place to give some. Each workflow's page has the same preview as a tab.

From the command line, a try runs on one record:

civex workflow try read-sample-time --record 3f2b8c1e
civex workflow try ./draft.yaml --record 3f2b8c1e --input files='*.csv'

A plugin of yours that reaches outside civex (a web request, a file of its own) still does that during a try.

docs.title: On and off
docs.text:
A workflow made in the app starts off: nothing starts it by itself until you turn it on, after trying it (Turn it on once the preview fails on none of its records, or on its page). An existing file without enabled: is on. Off, it still runs when someone starts it.

civex workflow disable read-sample-time
civex workflow enable read-sample-time

Both change only the file's enabled: line. To stop every workflow at once, see Stopping automation.

Any text editor works too: the app and the builder write the same file, and changes take effect on the next run with nothing to register. To share workflows with other computers, see the library. For your own steps, see Writing a plugin.

docs.title: Back up a project
docs.text: Goal: a copy you can restore everything from: records, history, settings and files.

docs.title: What makes up a project
docs.text:
my-project/
  _civex/
    config.toml     volumes, homes, retention, sync and other settings
    civex.db        the database (SQLite projects only)
    objects/        files on the default volume
    workflows/      workflow YAML
    plugins/        custom plugins
    exports/        export folders (can be rebuilt; skip them if you like)
/media/archive/civex/   any volume outside the project, one folder per volume

On PostgreSQL the database lives on the server instead of in civex.db.

docs.title: A full backup (SQLite)
docs.text:
1. Stop civex serve (and the desktop app) for this project, so the database isn't written halfway through the copy.
  2. Copy the _civex/ folder.
  3. Copy each volume folder that is outside the project. civex store list shows their paths.
civex store list
rsync -a my-project/_civex/            /backup/my-project/_civex/
rsync -a /media/archive/civex/         /backup/volumes/archive/

Stored files never change once written (they're named by their content hash), so after the first copy, rsync only copies new files.

Restoring: copy the folders back. If a volume ends up at a different path, point civex at it with civex store update archive --path /new/path. The volume's .civex-volume marker comes with it, so civex knows it's the same drive.

docs.title: PostgreSQL
docs.text:
Back up the database with PostgreSQL's own tools, plus the folders above (minus civex.db):

civex db status                         # shows the connection URL
pg_dump --format=custom --file civex.pgdump "postgresql://…"

docs.title: A portable copy: civex bundle
docs.text:
civex bundle export writes schemas, collections, records, the stored files the records cite, and the project's workflows and plugins to one file that any civex can read, whatever its database. Records keep their ids, so a record inside another, and one that references another, still line up in the project the bundle is read into. In the app it is Copy to another project… and Bring in from another project… on the Collections page. The copy can be put straight onto a drive of this computer (its exports folder), or downloaded.

civex bundle export --output backup.civex.zip
civex bundle export --no-files --output light.civex.zip   # records cite the files, bytes left out
civex bundle export --no-data --output structure.civex.zip # schemas and workflows only
civex bundle export --collection survey-2024               # one collection (repeatable)
civex bundle show backup.civex.zip                         # what a bundle holds

# into another project
civex init other-project && cd other-project
civex bundle import backup.civex.zip

Importing matches schemas and collections by name (one already there is reused, and a schema gains only the fields it lacks) and records by id (one already there, live or deleted, is left as it is), so a bundle can be imported again after more records were added. The import is one event in Activity. A bundle's plugins are code: read what lands in _civex/plugins/ before running workflows.

A bundle is not a full backup. It leaves out:

  • change history and Activity,
  • saved views and saved exports,
  • settings in config.toml,
  • files on a drive that can't be reached when it is written (the records still cite them; civex bundle show lists how many were left out).

A YAML dump written by civex dump in an older release is read by that release's civex restore; export a bundle from there.

docs.title: Projects that sync
docs.text: The authority holds the shared copy, so back up the authority as above. A device can be cloned again from it at any time. A device's identity (its key) is in ~/.civex/sync.toml, outside the project, and a copied project folder doesn't carry it: a restored device joins again with a new invite.

docs.title: Moving to another database
docs.text: To switch between SQLite and PostgreSQL, don't dump and restore. Use civex db move, which copies and checks everything, history included, before switching. See PostgreSQL.

docs.title: Cite the data in a paper
docs.text:
Goal: a paper (or thesis, or deposit) that says exactly which data it used, and a way to get that data back later.

  1. Make sure the data is as you want it, and on a synced project, that it has synced.

  2. Make a release on the civex hub that holds the project: Releases → New release. (Releases are published on a hub, never on a personal computer.) The files the records cite are kept where they are, not copied, so this is quick however much data there is.

  3. Copy the citation from the release's page (text or BibTeX). It names the version and the content hash, so a reader can tell whether the data they have is the data you used.

  4. If you deposit the data (Zenodo, a university repository), make a folder of it (Export… on the release's page): the files laid out by record, with manifest-sha256.txt, release.json and CITATION.cff. Upload that and the release's bundle (Download) and, once you have a DOI, add it from Edit details… on the release's page.

Later, to work with the data as it was, clone the release into a new project (civex clone <repo-url> --release v1). See Releases.

docs.title: Get files out as folders, zips or tables
docs.text: Goal: hand a set of files to someone, or open them in another program, arranged and named by their records rather than by hash, with a table of the records beside them if you want.

docs.title: What the folders look like
docs.text:
Files are laid out by the names of the records they belong to:

North Ridge/                      ← site
  2024-03-15/                     ← visit
    Sample 01/photo.jpg           ← sample, then its file
    Sample 02/photo.jpg
    Sample 03/photo.jpg
Samples.csv                       ← optional table of the records

Record names come from each schema's name template. Without one, a folder is named after the first value, which may just be 1. Set a template first if the folders should read well:

civex schema update sample --display-template "Sample {number:02}"

docs.title: 1. See what a selection of records holds
docs.text:
civex files list --in survey-2024

Path                                          Size  Where
North Ridge/2024-03-15/Sample 01/photo.jpg  195 KB  new-archive
North Ridge/2024-03-15/Sample 02/photo.jpg  195 KB  new-archive
North Ridge/2024-03-15/Sample 03/photo.jpg    1 KB  new-archive
3 file(s), 392 KB

Narrow it the same way for every command on this page: --in <collection>, --under <record id> (a record and everything beneath it), --schema, --field, --where field=value, --search, or --view schema/view for a saved filter. Add --paths to print where each file is on disk, for scripts.

docs.title: 2. Pick how to get them
docs.text:
You want… Command Takes space? A folder to open, instantly civex files export --in survey-2024 --name photos Only for files on another drive Copies you can edit, or on another drive … --name photos --mode copy --to archive Yes One file to send civex files download photos.zip --in survey-2024 Yes

A linked folder:

civex files export --in survey-2024 --name photos --table csv

/media/new-archive/civex/_exports/photos on new-archive: 0 copied, 3 linked, 0 already there,
0 removed, 1 table(s) written.
Linked files are the stored files themselves, so they are read-only (use --mode copy for files you
will change).
  • Links are free and instant. The folder goes on the drive holding most of the files; files on other drives, or on a drive that can't make links (exFAT, FAT32), are copied into it, and the room for those copies is checked first. To have no copies at all, move the files onto one drive first with civex files gather --in survey-2024 --to archive.
  • Linked files are read-only, because each is the stored file itself: a program can open them but not save over them. Use --mode copy for files you will change.
  • Running it again with the same --name updates the folder: new files are added and ones no longer selected are removed.
  • An unplugged drive: files that can't be reached are listed first and nothing is built unless you agree (or pass --allow-partial, which writes a MISSING.txt).

A zip, with the table inside:

civex files download photos.zip --in survey-2024 --table csv

Wrote photos.zip
      323  Samples.csv
   200000  North Ridge/2024-03-15/Sample 01/photo.jpg
   200000  North Ridge/2024-03-15/Sample 02/photo.jpg
     1000  North Ridge/2024-03-15/Sample 03/photo.jpg

docs.title: 3. The table
docs.text:
--table csv (or tsv, xlsx, json, jsonl) writes one table per kind of record. A file column says where that file is in the export, so the table and the folder always agree:

id,number,photo,taken_at,site
bfcdc007-…,1,North Ridge/2024-03-15/Sample 01/photo.jpg,,North Ridge
f75b804d-…,3,North Ridge/2024-03-15/Sample 03/photo.jpg,2024-03-15T09:30:00+00:00,North Ridge

--column (repeatable) chooses the columns, including a parent's fields (site) and fields through a reference (species.common). --no-files makes the table alone.

docs.title: 4. Save it to run again
docs.text:
An export saved with a schema is offered on every record of that kind and the kinds inside it:

civex schema exports add site "Photos, flat" --kind sample --field photo --layout flat --table csv

Saved site/Photos, flat: photo of sample · flat · csv table

Run it on a collection or within one record:

civex files export --export "site/Photos, flat" --in survey-2024 --name photos
civex files export --export "site/Photos, flat" --under 2d69dc46 --name north-ridge

Layouts: tree (a folder per record, the default), grouped (records holding files share one folder per kind: North Ridge/2024-03-15/Samples/…) or flat (one folder).

docs.title: In the app
docs.text:
Use the Export menu on any list of records, on a record's page, or on a collection's Exports tab. It takes exactly what the list shows, or the rows you ticked. From a list, it starts as the table on screen. Add files or more tables… opens the full builder (What · Finish), with a live preview of the folder tree; tick Put all the files in one folder beside it to drop the folder for each record. Finish with Save to a folder (any folder of this computer: Choose… opens the folder browser, and the choice is remembered) or Download a zip. A folder you chose gets ordinary files of your own. With none chosen the folder is a quick look inside civex: it opens at once and takes no space, and its files are read-only because they are the stored files themselves. Files on a drive that isn't plugged in are listed in the preview, with what to do, before anything is made.

Saved exports are on the Exports page in the sidebar. Its Made tab lists the folders made, with the space they use.

docs.title: Clean up
docs.text:
civex files exports list
civex files exports remove new-archive/photos     # as listed: where/name
civex files exports remove --older-than 30

Name        Where        Files  Links  Copies  Space   Updated
photos-copy  project      3      0      3       392 KB  2026-10-09 11:19
photos      new-archive  4      3      0       0 KB    2026-10-09 11:19

Removing a linked folder frees nothing and never touches the stored files. Anything of yours you added inside an export folder is kept.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Exports: layouts, tables in every folder, and the builder in detail.
  • civex files reference.

docs.title: Fill fields from file names
docs.text: Goal: instruments name files after when or where they were made (20240315_093000.csv). Have civex read that into a field every time a file is attached, so nobody types it.

docs.title: Set the rule on the field, once
docs.text:
A text, number, date or date-time field can carry a rule: fill me from this file field's name, with this pattern. From then on, whenever a record is saved with the file attached or replaced, the value is read from the file's name as part of the same save, before the field's own rules and the schema's unique keys are checked. So it works for a required field and for a field that must be unique, and nothing runs afterwards.

In the app, open the sample schema, pick taken_at and set Fill from a file's name: choose the file field (reading), give the pattern, and try it on a file name. From a terminal:

civex schema add-field sample taken_at --type datetime \
    --from-file reading --filename-pattern "YYYYMMDD[-_]HHmmSS"

Over the API the rule is a restriction on the field:

{"from_filename": {"field": "reading", "pattern": "YYYYMMDD[-_]HHmmSS"}}

Then attach a file and the field is filled:

$ civex record add --to survey-2024 --schema sample
  Parent record ID (visit): 2d69dc46
  number (integer) []: 3
  reading (file) []: /data/20240315_093000.csv
  taken_at (datetime) []:
Added record f75b804d-bff3-42a4-820f-30620587d84a.

$ civex record find --in survey-2024 --schema sample
ID         number  reading               taken_at
f75b804d…  3       20240315_093000.csv  2024-03-15T09:30:00+00:00

The rule follows the file, not whether the field is empty:

  • A blank field with a file is filled. Clearing the field and saving again fills it again from the file.
  • A different file fills it again. When the file is replaced (for a list, its first file; a new name counts, since the name is what is read), the value is read from the new name and replaces what the field held: the old value belonged to the old file.
  • With the same file, what you type stays. A hand edit is an override until the file changes. A value you give in the same save as the new file (or when adding the record) is yours too, and is kept.
  • A name that fits no pattern leaves the field as it is. A blank stays blank and a value stays; a new file that doesn't fit never empties the field. If a required field stays blank, the save is refused for the missing value, as it would be without the rule; otherwise you type the value yourself.
  • A name that fits but doesn't make the field's type (sample_ab for a whole number, a 13th month) refuses the save, naming the field, like any other value the field doesn't allow.
  • The value is held to the field's other rules (smallest and largest, allowed values) and to the schema's unique keys. A unique key filled from the file name is how a second upload of the same reading is caught at once.
  • A list of files gives its first file's name.
  • The file may be on the record above. A rule on a child schema may name a file field inherited from the parent schema; the name is read from the nearest record above that has the file, and only while the child's field is blank: replacing the parent's file doesn't reach into the records beneath it.
  • Records that already exist are not touched. The app's Fill from filename button on a record does one field by hand; for many records at once, see the workflow below.

docs.title: Patterns
docs.text:
A pattern is searched for anywhere in the name; it needn't describe all of it. It takes one of three forms:

  1. A token format (dates and times): YYYY MM DD HH mm SS stand for the parts of the date, year, month and day required; anything else is a regular expression, so [-_] takes a dash or an underscore. YYYYMMDD[-_]HHmmSS reads 20240315_093000.csv.
  2. A regular expression with named groups (dates and times, when the tokens can't say it): year, month, day, hour, minute, second, as (?P<year>\d{4}). A pattern that has named groups is read this way. (?P<day>\d{2})\.(?P<month>\d{2})\.(?P<year>\d{4}) reads 15.03.2024.
  3. A regular expression with a capture group (text and numbers): the first group ( ) is the value, or the whole match when there is none. site-([A-Z]+)_ reads NR from site-NR_2024-03-15.jpg.

Several patterns can be one rule: they are tried in order and the first that matches wins, so readings named either way are read by one field. Over the API pattern is then a list; the CLI takes the flag more than once:

civex schema add-field sample taken_at --type datetime --from-file reading \
    --filename-pattern "DDMMYYYY_HHmmSS" --filename-pattern "YYYY-MM-DD"
File name Field type pattern Gives 20240315_093000.csv datetime YYYYMMDD[-_]HHmmSS 2024-03-15 09:30:00 15032024_093000.csv datetime DDMMYYYY_HHmmSS 2024-03-15 09:30:00 site-NR_2024-03-15.jpg date YYYY-MM-DD 2024-03-15 site-NR_2024-03-15.jpg string site-([A-Z]+)_ NR sample_07.csv integer sample_(\d+) 7 depth_12.5m.csv float depth_([\d.]+)m 12.5

docs.title: Times are read in the collection's timezone
docs.text:
093000 has no UTC offset. civex reads it in the field's timezone, else the collection's, else UTC. For an instrument set to local time, set the collection's timezone first:

civex collection update survey-2024 --timezone Europe/London

docs.title: Renaming or deleting the file field
docs.text: Renaming the file field renames it in every rule that reads it. Deleting the file field drops those rules (the fields themselves stay).

docs.title: Once, by hand
docs.text: On a record with a file attached, text, number, date and date-time fields have a Fill from filename button. Give it a pattern and it fills the field. No setup is needed, and it works whether or not the field has a rule.

docs.title: Many records, or more than one step: a workflow
docs.text:
A rule fills a field as the record is saved. To fill records you already have, or when the value needs more than one pattern can give (several fields from one name, a lookup, a calculation), use the Value from the file name step (civex.value_from_filename@1) in a workflow. Save this as _civex/workflows/read-sample-time.yaml (or paste it into Workflows → New workflow in the app):

name: read-sample-time
description: Read the sample's time from its file name.
triggers:
  record_updated:
    schema: sample
    fields: [reading]        # only when the reading file is set or changed

steps:
  - id: extract
    plugin: civex.value_from_filename@1
    config:
      field: reading
      pattern: '(\d{8}[-_]\d{6})'      # 20240315_093000 or 20240315-093000
      output_type: datetime
      date_format: 'YYYYMMDD[-_]HHmmSS'

  - id: save
    plugin: civex.set_fields@1
    config:
      field: taken_at
    inputs:
      value: extract.value             # the extract step's output

The plugin reads names with the same tokens as the field rule, in two steps: pattern captures the part of the name, date_format reads it. See Value from the file name for every option. A workflow runs after the record is saved, so it can't fill a required or unique field in time; the rule above can.

To run it on records you already have, tick them in a list and choose Run workflow on N, or:

civex workflow run read-sample-time --record bfcdc007

The Runs page lists every run. A file whose name doesn't fit the pattern fails that record's run, with the reason:

  → workflow 'read-sample-time' (trigger: manual)
    ✗  plugin_error: Pattern '(\d{8}[-_]\d{6})' did not match filename 'sample1.csv'

From a terminal:

civex automation jobs --status failed
civex automation logs <job-id>

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Schemas and fields: every rule a field can carry.
  • Workflows: triggers, steps and inputs.
  • Automation: runs, failures, stopping loops.

docs.title: A spreadsheet
docs.text:
Goal: bring a CSV or Excel file into a collection as records.

Open the collection, choose New, then Import spreadsheet.

  1. Choose the file. It is sent as it is and read on the server, a part at a time, so a large file is fine.
  2. Say where each column goes: into a field the kind of record already has, into a new field (its type is guessed from the first rows, and you can change it), or nowhere. For a new kind of record, every heading becomes a field. To update records already there when you import again, choose the column that identifies a record, and whether a match is updated or left alone.
  3. Check: nothing is saved yet, but you see how many records would be added, changed or not saved, and why each row that won't work won't (a value that isn't a number in a number field, a date that isn't a date, a key repeated).
  4. Import. It reports its progress, and the whole import is one event in History, so the records it brought in can be undone from there.

Values are read as written: 007 stays 007, and a column is only taken for numbers or dates when every value in the first rows is one. If an import stops part way and a part is sent again, rows that were saved and have no matching column can be added twice: choose a matching column when the file may be imported more than once. Records that belong inside another record are not imported this way.

The wizard runs the Table and Save as records steps, so the same import can be scripted as a workflow, as below.

docs.title: A folder of files
docs.text:
Goal: turn a folder of readings, images or documents into records without adding them one by one.

A folder import is a short workflow, so it can be scripted and run again on the next folder: a workflow saved once is run from a record's page or the Workflows page.

Save this as _civex/workflows/load-samples.yaml:

name: load-samples
record_schema: visit            # run it on a visit
steps:
  - id: readings
    plugin: civex.files@1
    config:
      source: run              # chosen when it is run
      label: CSV files

  - id: insert
    plugin: civex.save_records@1
    config:
      schema: sample
      if_exists: add_new       # a record for every file
      file_field: reading
    inputs:
      files: readings.files

Then run it on the visit the samples belong to:

civex workflow run load-samples --record 2d69dc46 --input "readings=readings/*.csv"

Each new sample is created inside that visit. To read values out of the file names as well, see Fill fields from file names. For tables, the Table and Save as records steps do the same for CSV, TSV and Excel files; with Match on (or a unique key on the kind of record) a row updates the record already there, so importing the same table again changes nothing.

On your own computer, a Files step can read a whole folder instead (source: folder, or choose a folder in the run dialog): the files are read from disk where they are, nothing is uploaded, and files already stored are skipped, so it is much faster for many files.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Collections & records: adding records one at a time.
  • Schemas & fields: units, timezones and partial dates, which decide how imported values are read.

docs.title: Sync a project between computers
docs.text:
Goal: one computer (the authority) holds the shared copy of a project, and other computers (devices) work on their own copies and stay in step with it. Everything works offline: changes go when the authority can be reached.

This guide uses Tailscale to give the authority a private https:// address, because devices only connect over HTTPS. It is free for personal use and small teams, and needs nothing configured on the civex side. (Already run a server? Put any HTTPS reverse proxy in front of civex serve --sync-only --host 127.0.0.1 instead, and skip step 1. Can you SSH into the machine, such as a university lab machine? See Over SSH instead: nothing needs to run there.)

flowchart LR
    L[Laptop] <-->|https| A[Authority<br>lab-pc]
    D[Desktop] <-->|https| A

docs.title: 1. Install Tailscale everywhere
docs.text:
1. Install Tailscale on the authority and on every device, signed in to the same account.
  2. In the Tailscale admin console → DNS, turn on MagicDNS and HTTPS Certificates.

docs.title: 2. On the authority: accept a device
docs.text:
In the project folder:

civex sync authority enable
civex sync device invite laptop

This project now accepts devices. Invite one with `civex sync device invite <name>`.
Invite for laptop (shown once, works until 2026-10-10T11:08:28+00:00):

  civex_inv_tQyt6v66…  (the full invite)

This authority's key: RMLC-CDV3

Copy the invite now: it is shown once, works once, and expires after 24 hours (--hours changes that).

In the app: Settings → Sync → Other devices following this project → Accept devices, then Invite.

Without an invite: connect the device anyway (step 3 with no --invite). It shows a code like ABCD-2345 and waits; on the authority, civex sync device approve ABCD-2345 laptop lets it in (the app lists devices Asking to join in the same place; when the server has its own page, the device shows that address to open instead). civex clone <address> without --invite signs in the same way. civex auth status shows where a device stands. Handy when the device is in front of you and the authority is a terminal away.

docs.title: 3. On the authority: start the sync server
docs.text:
civex serve --sync-only --port 8100     # leave this running

In a second terminal:

tailscale serve --bg 8100

This prints the authority's address, such as https://lab-pc.tail1234.ts.net.

Point Tailscale at port 8100 only

--sync-only serves the sync API and nothing else. The full app (civex serve, port 8000) has no sign-in, so never expose it, and never use tailscale funnel, which publishes to the internet.

To use civex on the authority yourself at the same time, run civex serve as usual in another terminal.

docs.title: 4. On the device: clone
docs.text:
civex clone https://lab-pc.tail1234.ts.net field-laptop --invite civex_inv_tQyt6v66…
cd field-laptop
civex sync status

Authority   https://lab-pc.tail1234.ts.net
Project     84fbca56-a132-49af-939d-0bc1d820e168
Paused      no
Unsent      0
Conflicts   0
Files       keeps every file; 2 not downloaded yet
Last synced 2026-10-09T11:08:45+00:00

Records arrive first and the project is usable straight away. History and files follow in the background.

The device is joined from now on. It signs in with a key of its own, so it never needs the invite again.

In the app: Settings → Sync: paste the address and the invite, then Connect. To fill an empty authority from a project that already has data, connect that project the same way; it uploads everything.

docs.title: 5. Day to day
docs.text:
While civex serve runs on a device, it syncs by itself a few seconds after each change and every minute otherwise. Without the app open:

civex sync now       # once
civex sync watch     # keep syncing in this terminal

Received 2, sent 1

Keep the authority's civex serve --sync-only running (start it with the computer: a login item, Task Scheduler or a systemd service). While it's down, devices keep working and catch up later.

docs.title: 6. When two people change the same value
docs.text:
The authority's value stays. Yours is kept on your device until you decide:

civex sync now

Received 2, sent 1
1 value(s) did not go in as made; see `civex sync conflicts`.

civex sync conflicts

Id                                    Kind      What        Field  Yours        Theirs              State
9abf50d9-19ea-4f8d-88f7-c56e14eb5e5f  conflict  East Shore  name   North Ridge  East Shore (sulli)  open

Settle it with the id from that table:

civex sync resolve 9abf50d9-19ea-4f8d-88f7-c56e14eb5e5f --take mine   # or theirs
civex sync now

In the app: the status bar says when something is waiting. Review lists it, and each record's Resolve tab shows both sides side by side, with Accept theirs / Accept yours or an edit of your own.

Edits to different fields of the same record never clash: both go in.

docs.title: 7. Choose which files each computer keeps
docs.text:
By default a device downloads every file. For a large project, keep only what you work on:

civex sync files                  # per collection: here, not here, the setting
civex sync files opened           # default: fetch a file only when it's opened
civex sync keep survey-2024         # but keep this collection's files here
civex sync free archive-2019      # remove local copies the server holds

A file that isn't here downloads when you open or export it.

docs.title: Over SSH instead
docs.text:
If you can SSH into the machine that holds the authority, a device can reach it at an ssh:// address, the way git reaches a remote. Nothing runs there between syncs: each sync starts civex on that machine over SSH, and SSH carries the same sync API.

On the machine you SSH into (once):

uv tool install "civex[server]"        # civex must be on PATH or in ~/.local/bin
cd ~/projects/birds && civex init      # or an existing project
civex sync authority enable
civex sync device invite laptop

On each device:

civex clone ssh://you@lab-machine/~/projects/birds --invite civex_inv_…

The address is ssh://[user@]host[:port]/path. /~/ starts in your home folder, ?civex=/path/to/civex says where civex is if it is elsewhere, and hosts in your ~/.ssh/config work (ssh://lab/~/birds).

  • SSH must sign in without asking, since syncing runs in the background: use a key (an agent is fine). If the machine asks for a password or a code every time, share one connection (ControlMaster auto, ControlPersist 8h in ~/.ssh/config) and sign in to it once with ssh lab.
  • Accept the host key first: run ssh lab once in a terminal.
  • One machine at a time. Lab machines often share one home folder. While one serves the project it says so in _civex/open-on-host.json, and another refuses until two minutes after the last sync: two machines writing one database over a network drive can damage it. Use one machine's name in the address.
  • SSH forwarding must be allowed (it is by default). If an administrator has turned it off, use Tailscale instead.
  • civex there stops five minutes after the last request, and the next sync starts it again (about a second). CIVEX_SSH_COMMAND replaces ssh, as GIT_SSH_COMMAND does for git.

docs.title: Manage devices
docs.text:
civex sync device list            # devices, their key codes, waiting invites
civex sync device revoke laptop   # a lost laptop stops syncing at once
civex sync user "Dana"            # the name your changes are recorded under

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Syncing between machines: what syncs, the rules the authority enforces, sharing workflows, versions.
  • civex sync reference.

docs.title: Put files on another drive
docs.text:
Goal: keep a collection's files on an external or network drive, move the files already stored there, and later retire a drive without losing anything.

You need: a project with files in it, and the drive mounted (plugged in, or a network share your OS has already mounted; civex doesn't mount shares).

docs.title: 1. Add the drive as a volume
docs.text:
civex store add archive --path /media/archive/civex --allocated-gb 500

Added volume 'archive' at /media/archive/civex.
  Allocation: 500.0 GB
  Add it to the write queue with: civex store queue, or give a collection this volume as its home
with civex store place set.

In the app: Settings → Storage → Drives → Add drive. Browse… lists the folders and mounted drives of the computer running civex, and checks the folder before you add it.

civex writes a small .civex-volume marker into the folder, so the drive is recognised wherever it is mounted, and a different drive at the same path is never written to.

docs.title: 2. Send a collection's new files there
docs.text:
civex store place set survey-2024 archive

New files for 'survey-2024' now go to 'archive' (spill when it is unavailable).

Spill means that if the drive is unplugged, uploads go to the next volume in the write queue instead of failing. To refuse uploads instead, so the collection's files are never written anywhere else:

civex store place set survey-2024 archive --on-unavailable fail

In the app: Settings → Storage → Collections, and pick the home on the collection's row (or tick several collections to set them together).

docs.title: 3. Move the files already stored
docs.text:
Preview first:

civex store move --collection survey-2024 --to archive --dry-run

Would move 2 files (391 KB); 0 already on a target.
  → archive: about 2 files (391 KB), 2.7 GB free

Then run it:

civex store move --collection survey-2024 --to archive

Queued 4635f033. Ctrl+C pauses; resume with `civex store transfers resume 4635f033`.
Moving 4635f033  2/2 files  14 MB/s ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 100% 0:00:00
4635f033 consolidate  completed  2/2 files, 391 KB of 391 KB

Each file is copied, checked against its hash, and only then removed from where it was, so stopping at any point (Ctrl+C, a power cut) loses nothing. civex store transfers resume <id> carries on from where it stopped.

In the app: Settings → Storage → Tasks → Move files…. A running move shows in the status bar on every page, with Pause.

docs.title: 4. Check where the files are
docs.text:
civex store collections

survey-2024  2 files, 391 KB
  archive: 2 files, 391 KB

For one record:

civex store where bfcdc007

Field    File                 Stored on  State
reading  20240315_093000.csv  archive    online

docs.title: When the drive is unplugged
docs.text:
Nothing breaks. Records stay editable, and only the files on that drive are unavailable. Their chip in the app says which drive to plug in. New uploads spill to the write queue (unless the home is set to fail). Plug the drive back in and everything is available again, with nothing to run.

civex store list shows each volume's status, and below the table why a volume can't be used and what to do:

Status Meaning What to do ok Readable and writable — ⚠ low space Near its allocation or the disk is nearly full Move files off, or raise --allocated-gb with civex store update offline The path isn't there, or a network drive stopped answering Plug in or remount the drive wrong drive Something else is mounted at the path Mount the right drive. If it is the right one (re-formatted, marker deleted), run civex store adopt archive read-only / retired Readable, never written to Set on purpose with civex store set-state

docs.title: Retire an old drive
docs.text:
Move everything off it, then remove it:

civex store add new-archive --path /media/new-archive/civex
civex store move --off archive --to new-archive
civex store set-state archive retired
civex store place clear survey-2024        # or point it at the new drive
civex store remove archive

While a drive is being emptied it is made read-only, so new files don't land on it. It goes back to its previous state when the move stops. civex store remove only removes the volume from civex's settings and never deletes anything on the drive.

docs.title: Use a drive for every new file
docs.text:
The write queue is the order volumes are tried for files whose collection has no home:

civex store queue new-archive default

Write queue set to: new-archive → default

docs.title: Free space taken by unused files
docs.text:
Files stay stored after nothing uses them any more (a record was permanently deleted, a file was replaced). Clean-up removes them. It is a dry run unless you pass --apply:

civex store gc                          # what would go, on every volume
civex store gc --volume archive --apply # delete it, on one volume

Files used by a record, including one you can still restore, or by a workflow run are never removed. Files added in the last 14 days are kept too (--grace-days). In the app: Settings → Storage → Tasks → Clean up….

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Storage volumes: how copies, homes and moves work in detail.
  • civex store reference.

docs.title: Undo a mistake
docs.text: Goal: put back a value someone overwrote, or bring back something deleted. Every change is recorded, and deletes are reversible until you choose to purge.

docs.title: Put back an edit
docs.text:
Find the change in the record's history:

civex history record 2d69dc46

Entry     When              Action  Changes
077ba5fe  2026-10-09 12:09  update  Site: North Ridge → East Point
6d774cad  2026-10-09 12:07  create  Site: (none) → North Ridge

Revert it. civex shows what goes back and asks first:

civex history revert 077ba5fe
civex history revert 077ba5fe --field site        # only some fields
civex history revert 077ba5fe --force             # even fields edited since

A field that was edited again after that entry is left alone unless you pass --force. The revert is itself a change, so it can be reverted too.

In the app: the record's History tab, click the entry, then Revert…. It shows each field as it is and as it would become.

docs.title: Undo a bulk edit
docs.text:
An edit made to many records at once (Edit… in the explorer, or civex record set) is one line in Activity. Click Undo on that line and every record it changed gets its old values back, as one new event that can itself be undone. It says first how many records go back, which were edited again since (left as they are unless you tick the box to overwrite them), and which can't go back and why, such as a record deleted since.

civex history undo-edit --last          # the most recent bulk edit
civex history undo-edit --last --force  # even fields edited since

docs.title: Bring back a deleted record
docs.text:
civex trash list

Type    Name            ID        Deleted
record  1 in survey-2024  bfcdc007  today
Retention: 30 day(s). Restore with `civex schema|collection|record restore <name/id>` …

civex record restore bfcdc007

Restored record 'bfcdc007'.

A record comes back with the children that were deleted with it. To be choosy:

civex record restore bfcdc007 --only-this      # leave its children deleted
civex record restore bfcdc007 --with-parents   # also bring back deleted records above it

In the app: Activity in the sidebar → press Deleted → Restore on the row. A bulk delete is one row ("Deleted 71 records"): Restore brings all of it back, or open it and tick only the records you want.

docs.title: Bring back a field, schema or collection
docs.text:
civex schema restore sample
civex collection restore survey-2024
civex trash list --kind field                  # find the field's id
civex schema restore-field sample <field-id>    # values come back too

Restoring a schema or collection brings back the records deleted with it, not ones you had deleted separately before.

docs.title: When a restore is refused
docs.text: Message says Why Do its collection / schema / parent is deleted It would come back somewhere it can't be seen Restore that first (the app offers it) another record has these values A uniqueness rule would break Change or delete the other record a field with this name exists A new field took the deleted one's name Rename or delete the new field

docs.title: How long you have
docs.text:
Deleted items stay restorable until they are purged. Nothing is purged by itself. A clean-up you run purges what was deleted more than purge_after_days ago (30 by default), and only if that is switched on in Settings → Retention:

civex retention show

Purging (civex record purge <id>, Delete permanently) can't be undone and removes the record's history too, leaving only a note that it existed.

docs.title: See also
docs.text: • Deleting & restoring data: cascades, partial restores and retention in detail.

docs.title: HTTP API
docs.text:
Everything the CLI can do is also available over HTTP, served under the /api prefix by civex serve (paths below omit that prefix — see Server & web UI for how to start the server). This page is rendered from the same OpenAPI spec the running server exposes at /openapi.json, so it stays in sync with the code automatically.

The raw spec is also published alongside this page: openapi.json. Paste it into Swagger Editor, Postman, or an SDK generator if you'd rather work from the machine-readable version than this rendered page.

This reference doesn't include a "try it out" console — it's a static page with no server behind it, so there's nothing to call. Use civex serve and the live /docs Swagger UI for that.

docs.title: civex 2.3.3.post44
docs.text:
civex is a local-first research data management system: schemas, records, files, and workflow automation in one place, running on your own machine against your own database.

Every endpoint below is served under the /api prefix (e.g. GET /api/schemas); paths in this reference omit that prefix for brevity.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Errors share one envelope shape across the API. Domain errors (not found, already exists, validation, misconfiguration) return a 4xx/5xx status with a JSON body of {"detail": "<message>"}. Request body/query validation failures return 422 with {"detail": "Request validation failed", "errors": [...]}, one entry per invalid field. Anything unexpected returns a generic 500 with {"detail": "Internal server error", "request_id": "<id>"} — the same id echoed on the x-request-id response header, for correlating with server logs.

See the getting started guide for installing the CLI and standing up your first project.

Contact: James Sullivan sullivanj041@gmail.com License: PolyForm Shield 1.0.0

docs.title: POST /api/ai/chat
docs.text:
Chat

Request body

application/json 

{
    "messages": [
        null
    ]
}

docs.title: GET /api/audit/events
docs.text:
List Audit Events

Description

The whole project's history as events, newest first. A batch (an import, a delete that took a tree with it, a workflow run) is one event however many changes it holds, with a count of what it did; any other change is an event of its own, with its field-level changes and where the record is now. The filter and q match changes; an event is listed when any of its changes match, with how many did.

Import Bundle

Description

Read an uploaded bundle into this project. Schemas and collections are matched by name, records by id (one already here is left as it is); each record is checked and recorded in history like any other, and the whole import is one event in Activity. Plugins in the bundle are written to _civex/plugins/: they are code, so the answer counts them. A server without the plugin_install feature installs neither plugins nor workflow definitions: everything else is read in, and plugins_dropped / workflows_dropped count what was left out.
