docs.title: GET /api/collections/{name_or_id}/record-counts
docs.text:
Record Counts

Description

Record counts grouped by schema name — single SQL GROUP BY, no record loading. Takes the list endpoint's filters (except 'schema', which is the grouping), so e.g. 'within' counts what sits under one record.

Input parameters

Parameter In Type Default Nullable Description created_after query No Only records added at or after this instant (ISO 8601; no offset means UTC). created_before query No Only records added before this instant (ISO 8601; no offset means UTC). filter query No JSON-encoded filter tree, AND/OR groups of field conditions. Leaf: {"field": "", "op": "eq"|"ne"|"gt"|"gte"|"lt"|"lte"|"contains"|"in"|"is_null", "value": ..., "schema": ""?}. Group: {"and": [, ...]} or {"or": [, ...]}, nestable. 'value' must be a list for 'in' and is optional (default true) for 'is_null'. A leaf tests the listed schema's own field unless it names another 'schema': an ancestor's (tests the parent/grandparent record) or a descendant's (matches records having ANY such descendant that satisfies it). An inherited field name resolves to the ancestor that owns it. Example: {"and": [{"field": "status", "op": "eq", "value": "active"}, {"schema": "selection", "field": "selection_table", "op": "is_null"}]} name_or_id path string No parent_record_id query No Record id (or prefix): direct children only, of any schema. schema query No Only records of this schema. search query No Text to look for, case-insensitively, in the records' values: text, numbers, list items and file names (never field ids, file hashes or sizes, references or geometries). A record whose id starts with it (4 or more hex digits) matches too. search_field query array [] No Repeatable field name: look for 'search' only in these fields of 'schema' (required). Omitted, every searchable field. sort query array [] No Repeatable '[schema.]field[:asc|desc]'. Nulls sort last either way. A field needs 'schema'; 'schema.' names an ancestor whose field to sort by. '@kind', '@collection', '@updated_at' and '@created_at' sort any list, of one kind or of every kind. where query array [] No Simple equality filter, repeatable: 'field=value'. AND-combined with each other and with 'filter'. Kept for backwards compatibility -- prefer 'filter' for anything beyond plain equality. within query No Record id (or prefix): only records of 'schema' that descend from it, at any depth -- an encounter's selections, not just its recordings. Without 'schema', every record beneath it, of any kind.

docs.text:
Export Records Csv

Description

Export records in a collection as a CSV file, honoring the same filters as the record list endpoint. One table for everything listed; to choose the columns and format, or to take the files too, use POST /file-access/zip with a table.

Parameter In Type Default Nullable Description collection_name path string No created_after query No Only records added at or after this instant (ISO 8601; no offset means UTC). created_before query No Only records added before this instant (ISO 8601; no offset means UTC). filter query No JSON-encoded filter tree, AND/OR groups of field conditions. Leaf: {"field": "", "op": "eq"|"ne"|"gt"|"gte"|"lt"|"lte"|"contains"|"in"|"is_null", "value": ..., "schema": ""?}. Group: {"and": [, ...]} or {"or": [, ...]}, nestable. 'value' must be a list for 'in' and is optional (default true) for 'is_null'. A leaf tests the listed schema's own field unless it names another 'schema': an ancestor's (tests the parent/grandparent record) or a descendant's (matches records having ANY such descendant that satisfies it). An inherited field name resolves to the ancestor that owns it. Example: {"and": [{"field": "status", "op": "eq", "value": "active"}, {"schema": "selection", "field": "selection_table", "op": "is_null"}]} parent_record_id query No Record id (or prefix): direct children only, of any schema. schema query No Only records of this schema. search query No Text to look for, case-insensitively, in the records' values: text, numbers, list items and file names (never field ids, file hashes or sizes, references or geometries). Bulk Edit Records

Description

Set (or, with null, clear) these fields on every chosen record. Each record is saved as an edit of just those fields, held to the same rules as any edit and logged in its history; the lot is one event in Activity. It is saved a chunk of records at a time, each chunk whole and on its own, so other saves go in between two and a long edit never holds the database. docs.title: GET /api/records/count
docs.text:
Count All Records

Description

How many records match, in every collection. estimate=true answers from the planner on PostgreSQL (no scan: the same at a billion records as at a thousand); estimated says whether the count is exact.

Input parameters

Parameter In Type Default Nullable Description created_after query No Only records added at or after this instant (ISO 8601; no offset means UTC). created_before query No Only records added before this instant (ISO 8601; no offset means UTC). estimate query boolean False No Take 'total' from the query planner's estimate instead of counting (PostgreSQL; elsewhere the count is exact). 'total_estimated' says which it is. filter query No JSON-encoded filter tree, AND/OR groups of field conditions. Leaf: {"field": "", "op": "eq"|"ne"|"gt"|"gte"|"lt"|"lte"|"contains"|"in"|"is_null", "value": ..., "schema": ""?}. Group: {"and": [, ...]} or {"or": [, ...]}, nestable. 'value' must be a list for 'in' and is optional (default true) for 'is_null'. A leaf tests the listed schema's own field unless it names another 'schema': an ancestor's (tests the parent/grandparent record) or a descendant's (matches records having ANY such descendant that satisfies it). An inherited field name resolves to the ancestor that owns it. Example: {"and": [{"field": "status", "op": "eq", "value": "active"}, {"schema": "selection", "field": "selection_table", "op": "is_null"}]} parent_record_id query No Record id (or prefix): direct children only, of any schema. schema query No Only records of this schema. search query No Text to look for, case-insensitively, in the records' values: text, numbers, list items and file names (never field ids, file hashes or sizes, references or geometries). A record whose id starts with it (4 or more hex digits) matches too. search_field query array [] No Repeatable field name: look for 'search' only in these fields of 'schema' (required). Omitted, every searchable field. sort query array [] No Repeatable '[schema.]field[:asc|desc]'. Nulls sort last either way. A field needs 'schema'; 'schema.' names an ancestor whose field to sort by. '@kind', '@collection', '@updated_at' and '@created_at' sort any list, of one kind or of every kind. where query array [] No Simple equality filter, repeatable: 'field=value'. AND-combined with each other and with 'filter'. Kept for backwards compatibility -- prefer 'filter' for anything beyond plain equality. within query No Record id (or prefix): only records of 'schema' that descend from it, at any depth -- an encounter's selections, not just its recordings. Without 'schema', every record beneath it, of any kind.

Responses

    "estimated": true

docs.title: PUT /api/records/{record_id}/files/{field}
docs.text:
Attach File

Description

Add one file to a record's file field and save the record, as one request. The raw body is the file, streamed to storage as PUT /files/stream streams it; the record is then saved with the file on field (appended to a file_list, replacing the file of a file), so fields filled from the file's name, the field's rules, unique keys and workflow triggers all apply. A refused save (422, the field error as PATCH /records/{id} gives it) stores nothing: the content is removed again unless it was already in the store, and the record is unchanged. The file is placed as a file of the record's collection.

Input parameters

Parameter In Type Default Nullable Description field path string No name query string upload No The file's name. record_id path string No size query No The file's size in bytes, so a volume with room is picked before anything is written; the Content-Length is used when absent.

docs.title: GET /api/schemas/{schema_name}/records
docs.text:
List Schema Records

Description

List a schema's records across every collection -- the same query as a collection's list, just not scoped to one collection (what a saved view browses).

Input parameters

Parameter In Type Default Nullable Description child_counts query boolean False No Attach each record's live child count per child schema. columns query array [] No Repeatable column names whose values aren't in a record's own 'data' -- inherited fields and 'ref_field.target_field' joins -- returned under each record's 'derived'. created_after query No Only records added at or after this instant (ISO 8601; no offset means UTC). created_before query No Only records added before this instant (ISO 8601; no offset means UTC). cursor query No Opaque 'next_cursor' of the previous page: continue strictly after its last record. Costs the same at any depth and is stable while records are added or removed, unlike 'offset' (which it replaces; give one or the other). Sorted and searched lists page by it too. estimate query boolean False No Take 'total' from the query planner's estimate instead of counting (PostgreSQL; elsewhere the count is exact). 'total_estimated' says which it is. filter query No JSON-encoded filter tree, AND/OR groups of field conditions. Leaf: {"field": "", "op": "eq"|"ne"|"gt"|"gte"|"lt"|"lte"|"contains"|"in"|"is_null", "value": ..., "schema": ""?}. Group: {"and": [, ...]} or {"or": [, ...]}, nestable. 'value' must be a list for 'in' and is optional (default true) for 'is_null'. A leaf tests the listed schema's own field unless it names another 'schema': an ancestor's (tests the parent/grandparent record) or a descendant's (matches records having ANY such descendant that satisfies it). An inherited field name resolves to the ancestor that owns it. Example: {"and": [{"field": "status", "op": "eq", "value": "active"}, {"schema": "selection", "field": "selection_table", "op": "is_null"}]} limit query integer 50 No offset query integer 0 No parent_record_id query No Record id (or prefix): direct children only, of any schema. schema query No Only records of this schema. schema_name path string No search query No Text to look for, case-insensitively, in the records' values: text, numbers, list items and file names (never field ids, file hashes or sizes, references or geometries). A record whose id starts with it (4 or more hex digits) matches too. search_field query array [] No Repeatable field name: look for 'search' only in these fields of 'schema' (required). Omitted, every searchable field. sort query array [] No Repeatable '[schema.]field[:asc|desc]'. Nulls sort last either way. A field needs 'schema'; 'schema.' names an ancestor whose field to sort by. '@kind', '@collection', '@updated_at' and '@created_at' sort any list, of one kind or of every kind. where query array [] No Simple equality filter, repeatable: 'field=value'. AND-combined with each other and with 'filter'. Kept for backwards compatibility -- prefer 'filter' for anything beyond plain equality. within query No Record id (or prefix): only records of 'schema' that descend from it, at any depth -- an encounter's selections, not just its recordings. Without 'schema', every record beneath it, of any kind.

docs.text:
List Files

Description

A page of a selection's files, one row per file as stored (a file several records use is one row: uses lists those records, each with the names of the records above it, trail; others counts the records outside the selection that use it too), each with where it is (place: a drive's name, server or missing; place_kind: drive, unreachable, server or missing), narrowed by place, name (the name a file was added under, or its record or one above it, found as a search of records finds them) and the selection's own filter; and summary, where all of the selection's files are, by place. The counts and the order come from the database alone, so a page costs the same whatever it is a page of; only its rows are named. docs.title: POST /api/file-access/gather
docs.text:
Gather Files

Description

Move the picked files onto one drive: a selection's files, narrowed by place, name or ticked files (shas). Only those move; the rest of their collections stay where they are. Files only on the server are downloaded first; files on a drive that can't be reached, or missing, are left out. It runs like any other move (one at a time, safe to pause, cancel or lose power; see /store/transfers). Files downloaded straight onto the drive need no move: when nothing else has to move, transfer_id is null and downloaded says how many came. Every file picked goes, whoever else uses it: one on a drive that is the home of a collection using it is copied, so the home keeps it (plan.copied). With dry_run, only plan is answered and nothing is done. 422 when they are all already there.

docs.title: PUT /api/files/stream
docs.text:
Upload File Stream

Description

Upload a raw (non-multipart) request body, streamed straight to the object store instead of buffered in memory first. A multipart body sent via POST / has to be fully spooled to a temp file by Starlette's form parser before this code ever runs -- reading it back into memory here would mean the bytes touch disk twice for no reason. Sending the raw body instead lets us read it directly off the wire in chunks, and (unlike multipart, where per-part sizes aren't available upfront) a raw body carries an accurate Content-Length the object store can use to pick a volume with enough room before writing a single byte.

Input parameters

Parameter In Type Default Nullable Description collection query No Id of the collection the file is for. docs.title: POST /api/remote/connect
docs.text:
Connect

Description

Point this project at an authority. An empty project becomes a copy of it; a project with data fills an empty authority; two with data are refused.

The address, the invite and who holds data are checked before this answers (an invite is used up here: this computer joins the authority), so a mistake is said at once. Declare that the drive at the volume's path is that volume.

Volumes are recognised by an identity marker in their root, so civex can tell an unplugged drive from a different drive mounted at the same path. docs.text:
Try Workflow On Record

Description

Try a workflow (saved or not: the YAML is sent) on one record without keeping anything: it runs as a real run would, inside a transaction that is always rolled back, and the answer says what it would have done (each record created, changed or deleted, with the values before and after, and the runs its saves would start). JSON {content, record_id}, or a form with those plus the files for each files input. Works whether the workflow is on or off, and while automation is paused. 422 when the YAML doesn't pass its checks or the record isn't the kind it runs on; a step that fails is not an error but ok: false with error.

Null when it was not recorded. already_done For a synced batch, how many of its deletes the authority found already made by another change, and who made those. They are not counted in `count` and `parts`. batch What the batch was, for kind=batch. count integer Changes in it that match the filters. device For a synced change, the device it came through (verified by the authority). entry The change itself, for kind=entry. id string The entry's id, or the batch's. kind string entry (a single change) or batch. parts Array<AuditPart> For a batch, what it holds by kind of thing and action. docs.title: AuditLogResponse
docs.text: Name Type Description action string One of: create, update, delete, restore, purge. actor Who made the change, as reported by the machine that made it (the name chosen in the project, else the operating-system user). Not verified. Null for entries from before this was recorded. changes Array<AuditChange> What the entry changed, field by field, in schema order. A delete or purge lists the values that were lost; a restore lists nothing. device For a synced change, the device it came through, as the authority stamped it from that device's token (verified). Null for a change made on the authority, not synced yet, or synced before this was kept. entity_id string entity_type string One of: record, schema, field, dataset, view. id string new_data The thing after the change: whole for a create, identity and the changed values for an edit or restore (see `old_data`). Null on delete. now Where the record this entry is about is now, so a lost one can be told from one that was edited, deleted or purged. old_data The thing before the change. A delete has it whole; an edit or restore, which is stored as only what changed, has the thing's identity (id, name, label, where it sits) and the values it changed, so anything absent was not changed. A record's values are keyed by field id, so an entry survives a rename; `changes` has them by current name. Null on create. sync Array<> What became of this change when it was sent to the authority, if it did not go in as made: one row per clash, refusal or edit against a delete (kind, field_label, yours, theirs, base, theirs_actor, status, resolution, message, attempted, changes; the same rows as `/remote/conflicts`), open or settled. Empty for a change that went in as made, and when the project follows no authority. timestamp string(date-time)

docs.title: FileExportRequest
docs.text: Name Type Description allow_partial boolean Go ahead without files that can't be reached. Without it, a selection with unreachable files answers 409 and builds nothing. base A record (id or prefix) that paths start below; defaults to 'within'. below boolean Also take the files of every record beneath each selected one (the selected encounters, and everything inside them). Without it, only the selected records' own files. collection Only this collection. dest Advanced: a folder to build in, empty or an earlier export, instead of civex's own exports folder. Overrides 'name' and 'volume'. For 'link' it must be on the drive holding the files. export An export saved with a schema, as 'schema/name': its kind of record, file fields, filter, layout and tables become the selection, run in 'collection' and/or within the record 'within'. Sending 'layout', 'tables' or 'files' overrides what it has. fields Only these file fields; omit for every one. files boolean False takes the tables alone, with no files (needs 'tables'). filter A filter tree, as for listing records. kinds Only records of these kinds (schema names), when 'schema_name' is not given: how a preview of an export that takes any kind beneath a schema stays within that schema's own tree. layout string 'tree' puts each file in a folder per record above it; 'grouped' gathers the files of the records that hold them into one folder named for their kind (Encounter/Recording/Selections/...); 'flat' puts every file in one folder. Names that clash in a shared folder are told apart by the record that owns each. A saved view carries its own (files_layout); sending this with 'view' overrides it. mode string 'link' makes a folder on the drive holding most of the files: read-only hard links to the files there (no extra space) and copies of the rest. 'copy' makes real copies on one drive ('volume'), wherever the files are. name Names the folder: /exports/. The same name reuses the same folder. open boolean Show the folder in the file manager, if the request came from the server's own machine. record_ids Exactly these records (the rows ticked in a list); the other selectors are then ignored. schema_name Only records of this schema. search Text to look for in the records' values. search_fields Look for 'search' only in these fields of 'schema_name'. sort The order of the records, and so of the rows of a table: [{'field': name, 'direction': 'asc'|'desc'}, ...]. tables Also make these tables. Each file column in one says where that file is in the export. Sending it overrides the tables a saved 'export' has; an empty list removes them. view A saved view as 'schema/view': its filter, its file columns and its layout become the selection ('collection' and 'within' still narrow it). volume For 'copy': the drive to copy onto (a volume name); the project folder if omitted. Ignored for 'link', which goes where the files are. where Array<string> 'field=value' terms. with_within boolean With `within` and `schema_name`: also the files of the `within` record itself (a list of what a record contains, taking the record's own files too). within A record (id or prefix): its files and those of everything beneath it. Paths start below it. With 'schema_name', only that schema's records under it.

docs.title: Tags
docs.text: Name Description sync What an authority offers to the devices that follow it: handshake, push, feed, snapshot and files. For other civex installs, not people; only reachable remotely on an instance set to serve. schemas Define the shape of your data: schemas are named collections of typed fields (integer, float, string, boolean, date, datetime, file, file_list, reference), with restrictions (min/max, choices, accepted file types, ...) and optional inheritance from a parent schema. Create a schema before creating any records. collections Datasets are named containers of records that all conform to the same schema. Use this to create, rename, or delete the datasets you organize records into. records Create, read, update, delete, and bulk-import the individual rows of data that live inside a dataset. Record data is validated against its schema's field types and restrictions on every write. notes Notes on records, in threads: leave one, reply, resolve a thread. In history and sync; find what is open with the records' @open_notes filter. releases Frozen, citable copies of the data: a named version with a content hash, a citation, and a bundle that can be read back into a project. files Upload binary attachments (referenced from file / file_list record fields) and download them back out by content hash. workflows Author and manage YAML workflow definitions: chains of plugin steps, triggered automatically on record create/update or run manually, that read and write record fields. jobs Inspect the queue of workflow runs — one job per trigger firing or manual run — including their status, inputs, and outputs. audit Read the change history recorded for records, schemas, fields, and datasets — every create/update/delete with a full before/after data snapshot and timestamp. retention Clean up by age: deleted items, change history and finished workflow runs older than the retention settings or a given date. plugins Discover the built-in and project-defined plugins available to use as workflow steps, along with their declared inputs and outputs. Also handles uploading container-tier (Tier 2) plugins. ai AI-assisted helpers layered on top of the data model — schema suggestions, record extraction, and similar model-backed endpoints — plus the AI provider configuration they run against. remote Push and pull a project's schemas, datasets, and records to/from a remote civex server, and check the current sync status. store Manage the object volumes that back file storage — add, update, or remove a volume, and inspect per-volume usage stats. db Inspect and configure the underlying database connection: connection status, pending migrations, the configured URL, and (when using the bundled Docker Postgres) container lifecycle. Deliberately reachable even when the database itself is down. bundle A project's data as one file another civex can read: schemas, collections, records (ids kept), the files they cite (optional) and the project's workflows and plugins. Export one, say what one holds, or read one into this project. legal Read-only endpoints for the software's own license text and acceptable-use policy, independent of any particular project. status Live health checks, such as a round-trip database query, for monitoring whether a running server is actually functional. terminal A WebSocket-backed interactive shell in the project directory, used by the web UI's embedded terminal panel. logs Every log civex keeps on this computer (this project's server, the desktop app, its launcher, updates): their latest lines, downloading one, and opening its folder. update Updating civex itself from the app: whether a newer version is on PyPI, and updating and starting again. The update runs after civex has exited, so a running copy is never replaced. settings Per-project UI preferences, such as whether the Advanced navigation section (terminal, YAML editing, plugin editors) is shown by default. analytics Aggregate, filterable, time-bucketed reads over records, workflow jobs, audit events, and AI usage — the read path dashboard widgets call. Every endpoint shares one query-param filter contract (date range, dataset, schema, workflow_id, plugin_id, status, trigger); each documents which of those it actually applies.

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text: Generated from the civex command tree, so it always matches the installed version. Run any command with --help for the same information in your terminal.

docs.title: Command groups
docs.text: Group Commands Description civex ai 5 Configure the AI assistant civex auth 1 This computer's sign-in to the project's authority. civex automation 10 Manage automated workflow processing civex bundle 3 Move a project's data to another project as one file: schemas, collections, records (their ids kept), the files they cite, and the project's workflows and plugins. civex collection 8 Manage collections (named containers for studies or investigations) civex dashboard 3 The Analytics page: the cards everyone in the project sees civex db 10 Database management commands. civex files 8 Reach stored files by name and folder, the way the records are arranged civex history 7 See what changed, and when, and undo a change to a record. Entry ids are the short ones listed here. civex logs 4 See civex's logs: this project's server, the desktop app, its launcher and updates. civex plugin 3 Inspect available workflow plugins civex policy 2 View this project's data/governance policy documents. civex record 16 Manage records civex retention 3 Clean up by age: deleted items, change history and workflow runs. Nothing is removed unless you run it. civex schema 19 Manage schemas (data structure definitions) civex store 14 Manage file storage volumes civex sync 20 Keep this project in step with an authority: another civex that holds the project's shared copy. civex trash 2 Browse and manage soft-deleted schemas, collections and records (Recently Deleted) civex view 2 Saved filters: show, export civex workflow 5 Manage and run data processing workflows

docs.title: Top-level commands
docs.text: Command Description civex clone Make a new project that is a copy of an authority's, and keep it in step. Without an invite, this computer signs in as a device: it shows a code (and the page to enter it at, when the server has one), waits for approval, then copies. With --release NAME, make a new project from that release of the repository instead: a frozen copy, read-only by default, never in step with anything (over plain HTTPS the same as downloading the bundle and running civex bundle import). civex demo Create a demo project pre-populated with example schemas and records. civex desktop Open civex in a window of its own, with a project picker. civex doctor Check this civex install and, inside a project, its data. civex init Initialize a new civex project in the given directory. civex license Print civex's software license. civex release Releases are published on a civex hub, not made here. Take one with civex clone <repo-url> --release NAME; copy your own data with civex bundle export. civex resolve Identify a resource (schema, dataset, or record) by UUID or prefix. civex serve Start the civex HTTP API server. civex shell Start an interactive civex shell (no 'civex' prefix needed). civex shortcut Put a Desktop shortcut that starts civex for this project and opens it. civex update Update civex to the latest release.

docs.title: civex automation
docs.text:
Manage automated workflow processing

Command Description cancel Cancel one run. delete Delete runs, so a waiting one never starts. enqueue Manually enqueue a workflow job for a specific record. jobs List workflow jobs, with the fields that started each one. logs Show captured log output for a job. resume Lift a pause: triggers fire and waiting runs are picked up again. run Process all pending workflow jobs. Use --watch to keep polling. stats Show failed step-execution counts by plugin, across all jobs. status Say whether automation is paused, and how many runs are waiting or running. stop Stop all automation, for example a workflow that keeps triggering itself.

docs.title: civex automation cancel
docs.text:
Cancel one run.

A waiting run never starts; a running one stops before its next step.

docs.title: civex automation delete

docs.title: civex bundle
docs.text:
Move a project's data to another project as one file: schemas, collections, records (their ids kept), the files they cite, and the project's workflows and plugins.

Command Description export Write the project's data to one bundle file. import Read a bundle into this project. show Say what a bundle holds, without importing anything.

docs.title: civex bundle export
docs.text:
Write the project's data to one bundle file.

A bundle is a zip holding the schemas, the collections and their records with their ids, the stored files those records cite (unless --no-files), and the project's workflows and plugins. Read it into another project with civex bundle import.

Usage

civex bundle export [OPTIONS]

Options

Option Type Default Description --output, -o path civex-bundle.civex.zip Where to write it --collection, -c str Only these collections' records and files (repeatable); default all --no-files flag false Leave the stored files out (records still cite them) --no-data flag false Structure only: no records and no files --no-workflows flag false Leave workflows and plugins out --dry-run flag false Say what would go in without writing anything

docs.title: civex bundle import
docs.text:
Read a bundle into this project.

Schemas are matched by name (one already here only gains the fields it lacks), collections by name (one already here is reused), and records by id (one already here, live or deleted, is left as it is). Each record is checked and recorded in history like any other, and the whole import is one event in Activity. A record whose parent or referenced record is in neither the bundle nor this project is skipped and named.

Usage

civex bundle import [OPTIONS] BUNDLE_FILE

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description BUNDLE_FILE path yes A bundle written by civex bundle export

Options

Option Type Default Description --yes, -y flag false Skip the confirmation

docs.title: civex bundle show
docs.text:
Say what a bundle holds, without importing anything.

Usage

civex bundle show BUNDLE_FILE

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description BUNDLE_FILE path yes A bundle written by civex bundle export

Irreversible. restore Restore a soft-deleted collection (and the records cascade-deleted with it). show Show a collection summary with record counts per schema. update Update a collection's name, description, timezone or scope.

docs.title: civex collection create

civex collection create [OPTIONS] NAME

Option Type Default Description --description, -d str Collection description --timezone, --tz str IANA timezone such as America/Chicago. Datetime values without a UTC offset are read in this zone, and the web UI shows them in it. --scope str local 'local' (default): records here can only be referenced from this collection. 'global': records here can be referenced from every collection, for shared reference data such as species or sites.

docs.text:
Database management commands.

Command Description current Show the database's current migration revision and whether it's up to date. indexes List the field indexes in this computer's database. migrate Apply any pending migrations now, instead of waiting for the next connect. move Move this project's data to another database. moves List past database moves, newest first. revert Switch back to the database a move came from. setup-docker Set up a Docker-managed PostgreSQL container for this civex project. setup-postgres Configure civex to use a PostgreSQL database. status Show the database's connection, migration, and (if applicable) Docker container status. teardown Stop and remove this project's Docker-managed PostgreSQL container and its data.

docs.text:

docs.title: civex db indexes
docs.text:
List the field indexes in this computer's database.

A field is indexed when it is part of a uniqueness key or someone asked for it (civex schema index). Indexes are built and dropped in the background: by a running civex serve, or by a process that the command which changed them started. With --reconcile it is done here and now, showing progress. On SQLite a build gives way to anyone saving records, so it may wait for a quiet moment.

Usage

civex db indexes [OPTIONS]

Options

Option Type Default Description --reconcile flag false Build what is missing and drop what isn't wanted, now, showing progress

docs.text:

Usage

civex db migrate

docs.title: civex db move
docs.text:
Move this project's data to another database.

Copies every record, schema, collection and everything else into the destination, checks the copy against the original, and only then points this project at it. The original database is never changed or removed, so civex db revert can switch back. The destination must be empty or new; nothing is ever overwritten. The same steps apply whichever way you move: SQLite to Docker PostgreSQL, back again, or from one PostgreSQL server to another.

Usage

civex db move [OPTIONS]

Options

Option Type Default Description --to str Where to move the data: sqlite (a new file), docker (this project's Docker PostgreSQL) or postgres (a server you run). Asked if left out. --path str File to create, for --to sqlite. --url str Full connection URL, for --to postgres. Env: CIVEX_DB_URL. --host str Server host, for --to postgres. --port int 5432 Server port, for --to postgres. --database str Database name, for --to postgres. --user str User name, for --to postgres. --password str Password, for --to postgres. Env: CIVEX_DB_PASSWORD. --yes, -y flag false Don't ask for confirmation. --json flag false Print the outcome as JSON, with no progress bar or prompts.

civex db moves

docs.text:
Switch back to the database a move came from.

Nothing is copied back: records written to the new database since the move stay there. To carry those across too, move again into a fresh destination.

Usage

civex db revert [OPTIONS] MOVE_ID

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description MOVE_ID str yes Id of the move to undo (see civex db moves).

Options

Option Type Default Description --yes, -y flag false Don't ask for confirmation.

docs.title: civex db setup-docker
docs.text:
Set up a Docker-managed PostgreSQL container for this civex project.

Starts (or reuses) a named postgres:16 container, then updates _civex/config.toml with the new URL and creates all tables. The new database starts empty and your data is not copied into it: to carry an existing project's data across, use civex db move --to docker instead. Refuses to switch a project that has records to an empty database.

Usage

civex db setup-docker

docs.title: civex db setup-postgres
docs.text:
Configure civex to use a PostgreSQL database.

Auto-detects a local PostgreSQL server, creates the database and user role if needed, then writes the URL to _civex/config.toml and creates all tables. Pass [bold]--url[/bold] to skip interactive prompts (useful in scripts/CI).

Usage

civex db setup-postgres [OPTIONS]

Options

Option Type Default Description --url str Full PostgreSQL URL — skips all prompts. Example: postgresql+psycopg2://user:pass@host:5432/dbname Env: CIVEX_DB_URL.

docs.title: civex db teardown
docs.text:
Stop and remove this project's Docker-managed PostgreSQL container and its data.

civex init / civex db setup-docker create a per-project container that keeps running (--restart unless-stopped) even after the project directory is deleted. Run this before abandoning a project to avoid leaving it behind. Does nothing to a manually-managed PostgreSQL server.

Options

Option Type Default Description --yes, -y flag false Skip the confirmation prompt

docs.text:

Usage

civex files download [OPTIONS] OUTPUT

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description OUTPUT path yes Where to write it: a .zip, or the table's own file

Options

Option Type Default Description --in, -c str Only this collection --schema, -s str Only records of this schema --under, -u str A record (id or prefix): its files and those of everything beneath it. Paths start below it. With --schema, only that schema's records. --field, -f str Only this file field (repeat for several) --where, -w str Filter: field=value (repeatable) --search str Text to find in the records' values --view str A saved view, as schema/view: its filter, its file columns and its layout (--in/--under still narrow it). --export, -e str An export saved with a schema, as schema/name (see civex schema exports): its kind, file fields, filter and layout. Run it in a collection (--in) and/or within a record (--under). --layout str tree: a folder per record above each file (default); grouped: the folders above, but the records holding the files gathered into one folder named for their kind (Site/Visit/Samples); flat: every file in one folder. One of: tree, grouped, flat. --table, -t str Also make a table of the records, one per kind of record, named for the kind (Samples.csv). One of: csv, tsv, xlsx, json, jsonl. --column, -C str A column of the table (repeat for several, in order): a field, a ref_field.target_field join, or id/schema/created_at/updated_at. Default: the id and every field. --no-files flag false Make the table alone, without the files. --allow-partial flag false Go ahead without the files that can't be reached (MISSING.txt lists them)

docs.title: civex files export
docs.text:
Build a folder of the files, named and arranged by their records.

With --table FORMAT the folder also holds a table of those records (one per kind, named for it: Samples.csv, or .tsv .xlsx .json .jsonl), whose file columns say where each file is in the folder; --column picks its columns and --no-files makes the table alone.

Prints what can't be reached first. If anything can't (a drive that isn't connected) nothing is made unless you agree, or pass --allow-partial. With --mode link, files spread over more than one drive can't be gathered into one linked folder; use --mode copy --to for those. Running it again on the same folder updates it: new files are added and ones no longer selected are removed. A folder holding other files is refused, so nothing of yours is touched. Remove exports with civex files exports remove.

Usage

civex files export [OPTIONS] [DEST]

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description DEST path no Advanced: a folder to build in (empty, or an earlier export). Leave out to use civex's own exports folder, which civex files exports can list and clean up.

Options

Option Type Default Description --in, -c str Only this collection --schema, -s str Only records of this schema --under, -u str A record (id or prefix): its files and those of everything beneath it. Paths start below it. With --schema, only that schema's records. --field, -f str Only this file field (repeat for several) --where, -w str Filter: field=value (repeatable) --search str Text to find in the records' values --view str A saved view, as schema/view: its filter, its file columns and its layout (--in/--under still narrow it). --export, -e str An export saved with a schema, as schema/name (see civex schema exports): its kind, file fields, filter and layout. Run it in a collection (--in) and/or within a record (--under). --layout str tree: a folder per record above each file (default); grouped: the folders above, but the records holding the files gathered into one folder named for their kind (Site/Visit/Samples); flat: every file in one folder. One of: tree, grouped, flat. --table, -t str Also make a table of the records, one per kind of record, named for the kind (Samples.csv). One of: csv, tsv, xlsx, json, jsonl. --column, -C str A column of the table (repeat for several, in order): a field, a ref_field.target_field join, or id/schema/created_at/updated_at. Default: the id and every field. --no-files flag false Make the table alone, without the files. --mode str link link: hard links in a folder on the drive that holds the files, so nothing is copied (refused if the files are on several drives); copy: real copies on one drive (--to). A link is the stored file itself, so don't edit it in place. --to str With --mode copy: the drive (volume name) to copy onto. Default: the project folder. --name str Name of the export folder (default: from the selection) --allow-partial flag false Go ahead without the files that can't be reached (they are listed in MISSING.txt)

docs.title: civex history
docs.text:
See what changed, and when, and undo a change to a record. Entry ids are the short ones listed here.

Command Description collection Show what changed on a collection, newest first. compact Store history written before this version as what changed rather than two whole copies of a thing per edit. The server does this by itself in the background; this does it now, with a progress bar. Each entry is checked to read the same before it is rewritten, and stopping (Ctrl+C) loses nothing: running it again carries on. record Show what changed on a record, newest first. revert Undo a change to a record. schema Show what changed on a schema and its own fields, newest first. show Show one history entry with every change in full. undo-edit Undo a whole bulk edit, such as one made with civex record set.

Undo a change to a record.

An update puts the fields it changed back to what they were, a delete restores the record, and a create deletes it. Fields edited since are left alone unless --force is given. The revert is recorded in the record's history like any other edit, so it can be undone too.

A plugin declares its id, capabilities, inputs, outputs and config in its header, under [tool.civex], so civex knows it without running it. This runs the plugin once to ask, and compares. With --write it writes the header from the code's answer and locks the plugin's dependencies, so it runs exactly what was resolved now. Saving a plugin from the app does the same. Exits 1 when the header is missing or disagrees (without --write).

docs.title: civex record
docs.text:
Manage records

Command Description add Add a record, prompting for each field defined on the schema. check Check records for what needs a look: values their field's rules now refuse (a rule tightened after they were entered), required fields left empty, records sharing a unique key, links to records that are gone and files that are nowhere. delete Delete a record (and its children) to Recently Deleted. delete-all Delete all records in a dataset (optionally filtered by schema). find List records in a dataset. Use --schema to filter by type and show field columns, and --search to find records by what they hold. move Move records to another collection, or inside another record. move-all Move every record of a collection (or of one schema in it) to another. note Notes left on records orphans List live records that sit under a deleted record, so nothing above them lists them, with what they sit under. Put one back in place with civex record restore-above <id>, or delete it. purge Permanently delete a record that's already in Recently Deleted. Irreversible. restore Restore a soft-deleted record (and the children cascade-deleted with it). restore-above Bring back what a live record sits under that is deleted: each deleted record directly above it, by itself, so their other children stay deleted. set Set (or clear) fields on many records at once. show Show a record's field values. summarise Summarise records: group them by field values and work out counts, averages, totals and more over each group. update Update a record's field values, prompting for each field.

docs.text:
Check records for what needs a look: values their field's rules now refuse (a rule tightened after they were entered), required fields left empty, records sharing a unique key, links to records that are gone and files that are nowhere.

The records are those record find would list with the same options. Prints one line per kind, field and issue with a count; with --issue, lists the records that have it (their ids are what record set --id takes to put them right). Nothing is changed.

Usage

docs.title: civex record summarise
docs.text:
Summarise records: group them by field values and work out counts, averages, totals and more over each group.

The records are those record find would list with the same options. A date groups by year, month, week or day (one known only to the year keeps a group of its own), a date and time in its field's or collection's time zone, a number by value or in ranges, a list (tags, links) by each item. The last row is the totals over every record, each counted once.

Usage

civex record summarise [OPTIONS]

Options

Option Type Default Description --in str The collection (omit for every collection) --schema, -s str The kind of record to summarise (required) --by, -b str Group by a field (repeatable, up to 3): 'field', or 'kind.field' for a field of a kind above; add ':year', ':month', ':week' or ':day' for a date, or ':5' for a number in ranges 5 wide. --measure, -m str What to work out (repeatable): 'count' (records, the default), or 'filled', 'distinct', 'min', 'max', 'mean' or 'sum' then ':field', e.g. 'mean:depth'. --where, -w str Only records with field=value; repeatable --search, -q str Only records whose values contain this text --within str Only records beneath this record (id or prefix) --limit, -n int 1000 The most groups to show --format, -f str Print the summary as csv, tsv, json or jsonl instead of a table (a last row holds the totals). --csv flag false The same as --format csv

docs.title: civex retention
docs.text:
Clean up by age: deleted items, change history and workflow runs. Nothing is removed unless you run it.

Command Description forget-purged Delete the history of records that were permanently deleted. run Remove what is older than the retention settings or than dates you give. show Show how long each kind is kept, and what a clean-up would remove now.

docs.title: civex retention forget-purged
docs.text:
Delete the history of records that were permanently deleted.

Permanently deleting a record now deletes every history entry about it. This does the same for records that were permanently deleted before that was so. It cannot be undone.

Usage

civex retention forget-purged [OPTIONS]

Options

Option Type Default Description --yes, -y flag false Skip the confirmation prompt --dry-run flag false Only count

docs.title: civex retention run
docs.text:
Remove what is older than the retention settings or than dates you give.

Give --settings to apply the settings, and/or a date per kind (a date wins over the setting for its kind). It always counts first and asks before removing anything. History about something that can still be restored is never removed. Run civex store gc afterwards to reclaim files nothing refers to any more.

Usage

civex retention run [OPTIONS]

Options

Option Type Default Description --settings flag false Apply the retention settings (each kind left at keep-forever is left alone) --deleted-before str Permanently delete everything deleted before this date --history-before str Remove change history before this date --runs-before str Remove finished workflow runs and their logs before this date --yes, -y flag false Skip the confirmation prompt --dry-run flag false Only say what would be removed

Usage

civex retention show

docs.title: civex schema
docs.text:
Manage schemas (data structure definitions)

Command Description add-field Add a field to a schema. add-unique Require a combination of fields to be unique. charts The charts a list of a kind of record opens with create Define a new schema. delete Delete a schema (and the records typed by it) to Recently Deleted. exports Exports saved with a schema: which files, how they are laid out index Index a field in this computer's database, or stop indexing it. lint Report schema and field names that aren't valid slugs. list List all schemas. preview-formula Try a formula without saving it. purge Permanently delete a schema that's already in Recently Deleted. Irreversible. remove-field Remove a field from a schema. remove-unique Remove a uniqueness key (give the same fields it was added with). restore Restore a soft-deleted schema (and the records cascade-deleted with it). restore-field Restore a removed field, with the values records still hold for it. show Inspect a schema's fields (including inherited). unique List a schema's uniqueness keys. update Update a schema's name, label, description, or record name template. update-field Update a field's name, label, required flag, or restrictions.

docs.title: civex schema add-field
docs.text:
Add a field to a schema.

The field name is a slug because workflow steps reference it by name (e.g. a field: setting). Use --label for the human-readable version shown in the UI and in civex schema show.

Restriction examples: 

--type integer --min 0 --max 100
--type string --choices "left,right,bilateral"
--type string --max-length 255
--type file --accept ".csv,.txt" --max-size 10485760
--type float --unit m --min 0
--type date --precision month
--type geo --geometry-types Point --bbox "-12,48,4,62"
--type datetime --from-file audio --filename-pattern "YYYYMMDD[-_]HHmmSS"
--type formula --expression "mass / height ** 2" --decimals 1

Usage

civex schema add-field [OPTIONS] SCHEMA_NAME FIELD_NAME

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description SCHEMA_NAME str yes Schema to add the field to FIELD_NAME str yes Field name — the machine key used by workflows and CSV headers (lowercase, underscores, e.g. visited_on)

Options

Option Type Default Description --label, -l str Human-facing display name, free text (e.g. 'Visited On') --type, -t str Field type: integer | float | string | longtext | boolean | date | datetime | geo | file | file_list | reference | reference_list | tags | url | formula (required) --required, --optional flag --optional Whether the field is required --references str Target schema (--type reference) --min float Minimum value (integer/float) --max float Maximum value (integer/float) --choices str Comma-separated allowed values (string) --max-length int Maximum character length (string) --accept str Allowed extensions e.g. '.csv,.txt' (file/file_list) --max-size int Maximum file size in bytes (file/file_list) --unit str Unit every value is stored in, e.g. m or degC (float). Values are never converted after the fact. --precision str Least precise date accepted: year | month | day (date) --geometry-types str Comma-separated shapes allowed, e.g. Point,Polygon (geo) --bbox str Allowed area as WEST,SOUTH,EAST,NORTH in degrees; west greater than east crosses the 180th meridian (geo) --from-file str Fill this field from the name of the file in this file field when it is left blank (string, integer, float, date, datetime). Needs --filename-pattern. --filename-pattern str How to read the value out of the file name: for a date or datetime a token format such as YYYYMMDD[-_]HHmmSS (tokens YYYY MM DD HH mm SS, anything else a regular expression) or a regular expression with named groups year, month, day, hour, minute, second; for text and numbers a regular expression whose first capture group is the value. Give it more than once to try several patterns in order. --expression, -e str The formula (--type formula): field names, numbers, "text", + - * / // % **, comparisons, and/or/not, a if condition else b, and functions such as round(x, 2), days_between(start, end) and concat(a, "-", b). Worked out when a record is read, never stored. --result str What a formula gives: float | integer | string | boolean | date | datetime. Left out, it is worked out from the formula. --decimals int Decimal places for a formula giving a float

docs.title: civex schema add-unique
docs.text:
Require a combination of fields to be unique.

No two records of the schema may then hold the same values in all of the given fields, within the same parent record (or the same collection, for a top-level record). A record with a blank in any of them is not constrained. Refused while existing records already share values.

Usage

civex schema add-unique NAME FIELDS...

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description NAME str yes Schema name FIELDS... str yes The fields of the key (the schema's own)

The choice is a setting of this computer's database, never synced. The index is built in the background (a while on a big table; lists work meanwhile, only slower). A field in a uniqueness key is always indexed.

docs.title: civex store
docs.text:
Manage file storage volumes

Command Description add Add a new storage volume. adopt Declare that the drive at a volume's path is that volume. bucket Keep this project's files in an S3 bucket instead of on drives collections Show which volumes hold each collection's files. gc Reclaim object-store blobs no longer referenced by any record or workflow job. list List configured volumes and their current usage. move Move stored files between volumes. place Choose which volume a collection's new files go to queue Set the write queue (ordered list of volumes for new file writes). remove Remove a volume from the configuration (does not delete files). set-state Change what a volume may be used for. transfers Look at, pause, resume and cancel moves of files between volumes update Update a volume's path or allocation. where Show which volume each of a record's files is stored on.

docs.title: civex store add
docs.text:
Add a new storage volume.

The path can be on a removable drive or a network drive that is already mounted on this computer. Civex doesn't mount network drives itself: mount it first, then give the mounted folder.

Usage

civex store add [OPTIONS] NAME

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description NAME str yes Volume name

Options

Option Type Default Description --path, -p str Directory path for this volume (required) --allocated-gb float Max GB civex may use (omit for unlimited) --queue flag false Also add the volume to the general write queue.

docs.title: civex store adopt
docs.text:
Declare that the drive at a volume's path is that volume.

A volume is recognised by an identity marker in its root, so civex can tell an unplugged drive from a different drive mounted at the same path. If a volume is reported as the wrong drive but this is in fact the right one (the marker was deleted, or the drive was re-formatted), this rewrites the marker. Nothing else on the drive is changed.

Usage

civex store adopt [OPTIONS] NAME

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description NAME str yes Volume name

Options

Option Type Default Description --yes, -y flag false Skip the confirmation

docs.title: civex store bucket
docs.text:
Keep this project's files in an S3 bucket instead of on drives

Usage

civex store bucket COMMAND [ARGS]...

docs.title: civex store collections
docs.text:
Show which volumes hold each collection's files.

Lists, for each collection, the volumes that hold some of its files with how many files and how much space, and flags files that another collection also uses and volumes that can't be reached right now. Read from the catalog, so it is quick. With --volume it answers the other way round: which collections are on a given drive. To gather a split collection onto one volume, use civex store move --collection.

Usage

civex store collections [OPTIONS] [NAME]

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description NAME str no Show just this collection (default: every collection with files).

Options

Option Type Default Description --volume str Only collections that have files on this volume: what is on a drive.

docs.title: civex store gc
docs.text:
Reclaim object-store blobs no longer referenced by any record or workflow job.

Not a root: audit history and job step logs, which retain FileRef snapshots forever -- treating them as roots would leave almost nothing collectible. Old audit diffs may reference a sha256 that GC has since removed; that's the accepted tradeoff of running this at all.

Defaults to a dry run. Pass --apply to actually delete.

Usage

civex store gc [OPTIONS]

Options

Option Type Default Description --apply flag false Actually delete collectible objects. Without this flag, only reports what would be deleted. --grace-days int 14 Skip unreferenced objects written more recently than this many days, to avoid racing an in-flight upload whose record/job write hasn't committed yet. --show int 20 Max collectible objects to list individually --volume str Only clean up objects stored on this volume (default: every volume). --rebuild-refs flag false Recompute the file-reference table from every record and job before collecting. Normally unnecessary (it is kept current on every write); use it if the table may have drifted, e.g. after editing the database directly.

docs.title: civex store list
docs.text:
List configured volumes and their current usage.

Usage

civex store list

docs.title: civex store move
docs.text:
Move stored files between volumes.

Use --off to empty a volume, or --collection to gather a collection's files onto one volume. Each file is copied and checked before the original is removed, so stopping at any moment, even a power cut, loses nothing. Moves run one at a time: if one is already running, this one is queued behind it. Ctrl+C pauses; resume later with civex store transfers resume.

Usage

civex store move [OPTIONS]

Options

Option Type Default Description --to str Volume to put files on (repeat for several, in order). (required) --off str Empty this volume (repeatable). --collection str Gather this collection's files onto the target (repeatable). --verify-full flag false Read every copy back and check it (slower). --keep-writable flag false Don't make the source read-only while draining. --dry-run flag false Show what would move and stop.

docs.title: civex store place
docs.text:
Choose which volume a collection's new files go to

Usage

civex store place COMMAND [ARGS]...

docs.title: civex store queue
docs.text:
Set the write queue (ordered list of volumes for new file writes).

Usage

civex store queue NAMES...

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description NAMES... str yes Volume names in write priority order

docs.title: civex store remove
docs.text:
Remove a volume from the configuration (does not delete files).

Usage

civex store remove [OPTIONS] NAME

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description NAME str yes Volume name

Options

Option Type Default Description --force flag false Remove even if the volume contains objects (existing file references will become unresolvable)

docs.title: civex store set-state
docs.text:
Change what a volume may be used for.

Usage

civex store set-state NAME STATE

Arguments

civex store transfers COMMAND [ARGS]...

Update a volume's path or allocation.

civex store update [OPTIONS] NAME

Arguments

docs.title: civex store where
docs.text:
Show which volume each of a record's files is stored on.

A file is stored once however many records use it, so this is where its content is, not a copy per record. A file on a drive that isn't plugged in is listed with the volume's state.

Usage

civex store where [OPTIONS] RECORD_ID

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description RECORD_ID str yes Record id (a unique prefix is enough)

docs.title: civex sync
docs.text:
Keep this project in step with an authority: another civex that holds the project's shared copy.

Command Description authority Act as the authority for this project. conflicts List values that did not go in as made, with both sides. connect Point this project at an authority. An empty project becomes a copy of it; a project with data fills an empty authority. Two projects that both hold data are refused. Without an invite, this computer asks to join and waits for the admin to approve the code it shows. device Devices allowed to follow this authority. disconnect Stop following the authority. The data here stays as it is. fetch Download every file this project's records cite that isn't on this computer yet, now, with a progress bar. Stopping (Ctrl+C) keeps what has arrived; the rest comes later. files See, per collection, how many files are on this computer and how many are not on this computer, and whether it keeps a copy here. With a mode, set the default for collections that haven't their own (civex sync keep). free Free space: remove this computer's copies of a collection's files; they are fetched again when opened or exported. Only files the server confirms it holds are removed, never one another collection kept here uses, and the collection is set to fetch files when opened. interval Set how often the background sync runs. With 'never' it syncs only when you ask (civex sync now, or Sync now in the app). keep Keep a collection's files on this computer: what is missing is downloaded in the background while civex runs (or now, with civex sync fetch). With --opened, fetch them only when opened or exported. library Share workflows and plugins through the authority: publish them from here, install them from there. Nothing arrives by itself. now Send this project's changes and bring in everyone else's. pause Stop syncing until resumed. Changes keep being recorded. reopen Take back 'keep theirs': the conflicts are open again. (Putting your value back, deleting or sending again made an edit; undo that from history instead.) resolve Settle a conflict, or with --all every open one. resume Start syncing again. send Upload the files this project's records cite that the server lacks, now, with a progress bar. Records sync separately (civex sync now); stopping (Ctrl+C) keeps what has gone up, and the rest goes later. status Show where this project stands with its authority. user Show or set the author name recorded on changes in this project. It is saved in this project's config.toml; the default is your operating-system user. watch Keep syncing in this terminal until stopped (Ctrl+C): after edits, on the interval, and backing off when the authority can't be reached.

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description URL str yes The authority's address: https://civex.example.com, or ssh://you@lab-machine/~/projects/birds to reach a project on a machine you can SSH into (nothing needs to be running there).

Options

Option Type Default Description --invite str The invite the authority's admin gave. Leave out when this computer has joined that address before, or to ask to join: a code is shown for the admin to approve on the server (civex sync device approve). Env: CIVEX_SYNC_INVITE.

docs.title: civex sync now
docs.text:
Send this project's changes and bring in everyone else's.

Records only: files go on their own, so a large file never holds up a change. The app and civex sync watch send them in the background; civex sync send sends them now.

docs.title: civex sync pause

docs.title: civex sync reopen
docs.text:

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description CONFLICT_IDS... str yes The ids of conflicts settled by keeping theirs.

docs.title: civex sync resolve
docs.text:
Settle a conflict, or with --all every open one.

Usage

civex sync resolve [OPTIONS] [CONFLICT_ID]

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description CONFLICT_ID str no The conflict's id (not with --all).

Options

Option Type Default Description --take str 'theirs' keeps what the authority has; 'mine' puts your value back as a new edit; 'value' puts the one given with --value; 'delete' deletes a record that was deleted there; 'retry' sends a refused change again from the record as it is now; 'restore_above' brings back the deleted records a refused record sits under, then sends it again. (required) --value str With --take value: the value to put in, as JSON (a number, true, a list, "quoted text"), or plain text. --force flag false Put your value back even though the record's value has changed again since the conflict was recorded. --all flag false Settle every open conflict that offers this way (narrow it with --kind), not one. Those that don't, or fail their checks, stay open. --kind str With --all: only this kind (conflict, rejected, edit_vs_delete or unfit).

docs.title: Top-level commands
docs.text:
Commands invoked directly as civex <command>, grouped the same way civex --help groups them.

Start a working area Description demo Create a demo project pre-populated with example schemas and records. desktop Open civex in a window of its own, with a project picker. init Initialize a new civex project in the given directory. license Print civex's software license. shortcut Put a Desktop shortcut that starts civex for this project and opens it. update Update civex to the latest release. Work on the current change Description doctor Check this civex install and, inside a project, its data. resolve Identify a resource (schema, dataset, or record) by UUID or prefix. Collaborate Description clone Make a new project that is a copy of an authority's, and keep it in step. Without an invite, this computer signs in as a device: it shows a code (and the page to enter it at, when the server has one), waits for approval, then copies. With --release NAME, make a new project from that release of the repository instead: a frozen copy, read-only by default, never in step with anything (over plain HTTPS the same as downloading the bundle and running civex bundle import). release Releases are published on a civex hub, not made here. Take one with civex clone <repo-url> --release NAME; copy your own data with civex bundle export. serve Start the civex HTTP API server. Other Description shell Start an interactive civex shell (no 'civex' prefix needed).

civex shortcut

docs.title: civex update
docs.text:
Update civex to the latest release.

Detects whether civex was installed with pipx, uv tool or pip and runs the matching upgrade. Other civex serve running from the same copy are stopped first and started again afterwards, after asking.

Pre-releases are only installed with --pre. Once on one, a plain civex update moves on when the final release is out.

Usage

civex update [OPTIONS]

Options

Option Type Default Description --check flag false Only report whether a newer version exists. --pre flag false Include pre-releases (release candidates, betas) when looking for a newer version. --yes, -y flag false Stop other servers running from this copy without asking (they start again afterwards).

docs.title: civex doctor
docs.text:
Check this civex install and, inside a project, its data.

The install checks look for another copy of civex shadowing this one on PATH, for uv, and for a working Python for custom plugins. The project checks look for integrity issues: dangling reference/reference_list values left over from before deletes checked for referrers, and live records that sit under a deleted record (out of sight; civex record restore-above puts one back in place). It checks the database has every table and column this civex expects, whatever revision it is stamped at. It also warns when the project keeps its files in a bucket but files are still recorded on drives, out of reach.

With --fix, deletes cached plugin environments that point at a Python that no longer exists (uv rebuilds them the next time the plugin runs).

Usage

civex doctor [OPTIONS]

Options

Option Type Default Description --fix flag false Remove cached plugin environments whose Python is gone.

docs.title: civex clone
docs.text:
Make a new project that is a copy of an authority's, and keep it in step. Without an invite, this computer signs in as a device: it shows a code (and the page to enter it at, when the server has one), waits for approval, then copies. With --release NAME, make a new project from that release of the repository instead: a frozen copy, read-only by default, never in step with anything (over plain HTTPS the same as downloading the bundle and running civex bundle import).

Usage

civex clone [OPTIONS] URL [PATH]

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description URL str yes The authority's address. PATH path no Where to put the copy (default: a new folder here).

Options

Option Type Default Description --invite str The invite the authority's admin gave. Leave out to sign in: a code is shown to approve, and the copy starts once it is. Env: CIVEX_SYNC_INVITE. --release str Instead of following the repository, make a new project from one of its releases: its bundle, with the files, is downloaded and read in. Nothing is connected and nothing syncs. --token str With --release: the host's access token, for a private repository. Env: CIVEX_TOKEN. --writable flag false With --release: allow changes to the new project (it starts read-only, a copy to read and cite).

Option Type Default Description --host str 127.0.0.1 Bind address --port, -p int 8000 Port --reload flag false Auto-reload on code changes (dev mode) --allow-remote flag false Permit binding to a non-loopback address. The server has NO authentication — only use this on a trusted network behind a reverse proxy or firewall. --log-level str INFO Log level: DEBUG | INFO | WARNING | ERROR. Overrides [logging] in config.toml. --open flag false Open the browser once the server is up. If civex is already running on this port, just open the browser. --sync-only flag false Serve only what devices following this project call, for an authority on a network: point the HTTPS proxy at this, and run the app itself on this machine.

docs.title: civex workflow
docs.text:
Manage and run data processing workflows

Command Description disable Switch a workflow off: its triggers start nothing, and it runs only when someone starts or tries it. enable Switch a workflow on, so its triggers start runs. list List all workflow definitions in _civex/workflows/. run Run a workflow against a specific record. try Try a workflow on a record without keeping anything it does.
