docs.text:
Switch a workflow off: its triggers start nothing, and it runs only when someone starts or tries it.

Usage

civex workflow disable STEM

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description STEM str yes Workflow filename stem

docs.title: civex workflow enable
docs.text:
Switch a workflow on, so its triggers start runs.

Usage

civex workflow enable STEM

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description STEM str yes Workflow filename stem

docs.title: civex workflow list
docs.text:
List all workflow definitions in _civex/workflows/.

Usage

civex workflow list

docs.title: civex workflow run
docs.text:
Run a workflow against a specific record.

What the workflow asks for when run is given with --input name=value: a Files step set to "chosen when the workflow is run" is named by its step id, and its value is a glob pattern (e.g. --input wav-files=*.wav).

Usage

civex workflow run [OPTIONS] NAME

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description NAME str yes Workflow name or filename stem

Options

Option Type Default Description --record, -r str Record ID or short prefix (required) --input, -i str Workflow input as name=value. For 'files' inputs, value is a glob pattern.

docs.title: civex workflow try
docs.text:
Try a workflow on a record without keeping anything it does.

It runs as a real run would, then everything it wrote is undone, and what it would have done is printed: the records it would create, change or delete, with each value before and after, and the runs its saves would start. Works whether the workflow is on or off. A plugin that reaches outside civex (a web request, a file of its own) still does so.

Usage

civex workflow try [OPTIONS] NAME

Arguments

Argument Type Required Description NAME str yes Workflow name, filename stem, or a path to a YAML file

Options

Option Type Default Description --record, -r str Record ID or short prefix (required) --input, -i str Workflow input as name=value. For 'files' inputs, value is a glob pattern.

docs.title: civex.files@1 (Files)
docs.text:
Bring files into a workflow. Where the files come from (source) is one of:

  • Chosen when the workflow is run (run): whoever runs it drops files in, or points at a folder on this computer. This replaces the old workflow-level inputs: {x: {type: files}}. The step's id names it in the run dialog, the command line (--input <id>=*.wav) and the API; What to ask for (label) is what the person sees.
  • A folder on this computer (folder): the files of folder that match glob (*.wav), optionally with subfolders. The computer running civex reads them itself, so nothing is uploaded and a run shows how far it has got. Files whose content is already stored are not copied again, so reading the same folder twice is quick. Hidden files (names starting with a dot) are skipped. A server that hosts other people's projects does not offer this (server_path_import is a feature of a computer's own civex, off on a hub).
  • A field of this record (field): the file, or files, in a file or file-list field of the record the workflow runs on.

Plugin ID: civex.files@1 Category: bring-in Capabilities: read, store_folder

Config

Field Type Required Default Description source string no run run: picked each time the workflow is run. folder: the folder named in folder. field: the files in the record's field. label string | null no null What the person running the workflow is asked for, e.g. 'Sequence WAV files'. folder string | null no null The folder on this computer to read files from (source: folder). Reading a folder is not offered by a server hosting other people's projects. glob string no * Which files in the folder to take, e.g. *.wav. subfolders boolean no False Also take files in the folders inside the folder. field string | null no null The file or files field of the record the workflow runs on (source: field).

Inputs

Name Type Required Description provided any no What was chosen when the workflow was run. Filled in by civex; leave it out.

Outputs

Name Type Required Description files files yes The files brought in. 
- id: wavs
  plugin: civex.files@1
  config:
    source: run
    label: Sequence WAV files

- id: put
  plugin: civex.save_records@1
  config:
    schema: sequence_selection
    match_on: [selection_number]
    filename_pattern: 'sel_(\d+)'
    file_field: seq_wav_file
  inputs:
    files: wavs.files

docs.title: civex.save_records@1 (Save as records)
docs.text:
Save the rows of a table or a set of files as records, one record for each row or file. When a matching record already exists, If a matching record already exists (if_exists) says what happens:

if_exists A row or file whose record is there One whose record is not update (default) changes the record, only what the table or file brings makes a record skip leaves the record as it is (counted in skipped, named in skipped_rows) makes a record add_new never looks for a match: always makes another record makes a record

Running the same table or files again changes nothing: the records are matched, found unchanged (unchanged), left without history and without starting any workflow.

Give it either rows (from Table) or files (from Files), not both.

Plugin ID: civex.save_records@1 Category: save Capabilities: read, write_records

Config

Field Type Required Default Description schema string yes The kind of record to save. In the YAML, schema:. if_exists string no update update: change the record, only what the table or file brings. skip: leave it as it is. add_new: always make a new record, never looking for a match. match_on array no The field(s) a row or file and a record must agree on to be the same record. For a table, empty means the kind's first unique key, or, when it has none, every row makes a new record. For files, one field, compared with the key in the file's name. filename_pattern string | null no null Files only: which part of a file's name says which record it belongs to, with one capture group, e.g. sel_(\d+). Build it from an example. file_field string | null no null Files only: the file field of each record. field_mapping object no Tables only: maps table column names to field names. Empty means columns are used as field names directly. as_written boolean no False Tables only: every cell is the text it shows. Blank cells are left out and each other cell becomes the value its field holds (a whole number, a date, yes or no); a row with a cell that can't be that is skipped and named. first_row integer no 1 Tables only: the number said of the first row when a row is named (2 for the first row under a heading row). dataset string no "" Collection to save records in. Empty: the collection of the record the workflow runs on. parent_record_id string no "" The record to match within and save inside. Empty: the record the workflow runs on.

Inputs

Name Type Required Description rows table no The table to save, one record for each row. Its columns go into the fields of the same name, unless Columns to fields says otherwise. files files no The files to save, one record for each file, with the file in the field chosen in Put the file in field. earlier table no Rows that come before the table, already dealt with (same columns): their keys count when a repeated one is looked for, so a table saved in parts treats repeats as one saved whole. Nothing is saved from them.

Outputs

Name Type Required Description created number yes How many records it made. updated number yes How many existing records it changed. unchanged number yes How many existing records already held what was brought. skipped number yes How many rows or files were not saved. skipped_rows list yes Why each row or file not saved was left out: no value to match by, a value repeated, several records with it, a matching record left alone, or a value the record refused. unmatched list no Files with no key in their name, or whose record could not be saved. ambiguous list no Files left alone because another file in the same run has the same key (one record holds one file), each with the files it clashes with.

docs.title: Tables
docs.text:
- id: sheet
  plugin: civex.table@1
  config:
    field: sample_sheet

- id: save
  plugin: civex.save_records@1
  config:
    schema: Sample
    dataset: survey-2024
    match_on: [number]
    field_mapping:
      "Taken at": taken_at
      "Depth (m)": depth
      "Sample": number
  inputs:
    rows: sheet.table

docs.title: How a row finds its record
docs.text:
Match on (match_on) names the fields a row and a record must agree on to be the same record. They are the kind's own fields, named after Columns to fields (field_mapping) is applied (number above, not the column Sample). A row is matched only against records of that kind inside the same record (Inside record, else the record the workflow runs on), in the collection it writes to.

  • Left empty, the kind's first unique key is used (the run log says so).
  • Left empty on a kind with no unique key, every row makes a new record.

Values are compared the way a unique key compares them: a number by its value (12 and 12.0 are the same; a column with a blank cell reaches the step as decimals), so a table re-read from the same file always finds its records. A number given for a text field is written and matched as its text ("12").

docs.title: What an update keeps
docs.text: An update changes only the columns in the table. Every other field on the matched record (a file, values computed by another workflow) is left exactly as it is, and an empty cell leaves its field alone instead of clearing it.

docs.title: Rows it leaves out
docs.text:
A row is skipped, counted in skipped and named in skipped_rows (the run shows them as problems), when:

  • a field it is matched by is empty in that row;
  • its key repeats an earlier row of the same table (the first is saved; the step never guesses which of two rows is right);
  • several records already have its key;
  • if_exists is skip and its record is there;
  • the record refuses its values (a restriction, a required field, a unique key).

The other rows are saved.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
- id: wavs
  plugin: civex.files@1
  config:
    source: run
    label: Sequence WAV files

- id: put
  plugin: civex.save_records@1
  config:
    schema: sequence_selection
    if_exists: update
    match_on: [selection_number]       # compared with the key in the file name
    filename_pattern: 'sel_(\d+)'      # one capture group: the key
    file_field: seq_wav_file           # where the file goes
  inputs:
    files: wavs.files

The key in each file's name (filename_pattern) is a regular expression with one capture group; the captured text is compared with the one Match on field (01 and 1 are the same number). Put the file in field (file_field) is a file or file-list field: a file-list field gets the file added (once; the same content is never added twice), a file field holds the file itself. A file whose key matches no record makes one, with the key in the match field.

  • With add_new, no key is needed: every file makes a record (the pattern, if given, still fills the match field).
  • Two files in one run with the same key are not attached (one record holds one file): they are listed in ambiguous, and nothing wrong is written. That is almost always a pattern that reads too little of the name (sel_(\d{2}) takes 14 from both selection 14 and 149).
  • A file whose name has no key is listed in unmatched, with files whose record could not be saved.

docs.title: civex.set_fields@1 (Set fields on this record)
docs.text:
Fill in fields of the record the workflow runs on. Only the fields named change; every other field is kept, and nothing is written (so nothing is triggered) when the record already holds the values.

Each value in fields is what you type, or {from_field: other_field} to copy another field of the same record. Values worked out by earlier steps can come in through the inputs: value (one value, put in the field named in field) and updates (several, as field: value; empty values are left alone, so a missing value never clears a field).

Plugin ID: civex.set_fields@1 Category: save Capabilities: read, write_records

Config

Field Type Required Default Description fields object no The fields to set and what to put in each: a value, or {from_field: other_field} to copy another field of this record. field string | null no null The field that the value input is put in.

Inputs

Name Type Required Description value any no One value, put in the field named in the Field setting. updates mapping no Several values, by field (field: value). Empty values are left alone. 
- id: copy
  plugin: civex.set_fields@1
  config:
    fields:
      status: reviewed
      summary: {from_field: condition}

- id: when
  plugin: civex.value_from_filename@1
  config:
    field: reading
    pattern: '(\d{8}[-_]\d{6})'
    output_type: datetime
    date_format: 'YYYYMMDD[-_]HHmmSS'

- id: save
  plugin: civex.set_fields@1
  config:
    field: taken_at
  inputs:
    value: when.value

docs.title: Taking a setting from a field of the record
docs.text: This is not special to this step: any setting of any step may be written as {from_field: name}. When the step runs, civex reads that field of the record the workflow runs on (as it is by then: an earlier step may have just set it) and uses it. A field with nothing in it stops the step with a message saying so. (This replaces the old "Read a field" step.)

docs.title: civex.table@1 (Table)
docs.text:
Read a table from a spreadsheet or text file: CSV, TSV or Excel (.xlsx). The file comes from a Files step (connect its files output to this step's files input) or, with no input, from a file field of the record the workflow runs on (field). Several files are read and their rows put one after another.

Its output, table, feeds Save as records (rows).

Uses pandas, which ships with civex. It is imported when the step runs, so the step registers quickly without loading pandas.

Plugin ID: civex.table@1 Category: bring-in Capabilities: read

Config

Field Type Required Default Description field string | null no null A file field of the record the workflow runs on. Not needed when files are given by a Files step. delimiter string no auto Column separator of a text file: auto (commas, tabs or semicolons, whichever the file uses), one character, or a name (comma, tab, semicolon, pipe, space). Used when delimiters isn't set. Excel files need none. delimiters array | null no null Several separators the file may use, such as [comma, tab] to read both CSV and TSV files. The one the file's own lines use is picked; a file using none of them is read with the first. Overrides delimiter. encoding string no utf-8 Text encoding to decode a text file with. sheet string | null no null Which sheet of an Excel file to read, by name. The first sheet when empty. as_text boolean no False Read every cell as the text it shows, with nothing guessed: 007 stays 007, a blank cell is empty text. Off: numbers, dates and yes/no are worked out from the file. skip_rows integer no 0 Leave out this many rows after the heading row, to read a large file a part at a time. max_rows integer | null no null Stop after this many rows (after any skipped). All of them when empty. only_columns array | null no null Read just the columns with these headings. All of them when empty.

Inputs

Name Type Required Description files files no The file (or files, whose rows are put one after another) to read. Leave out to read the file in the Field setting.

Outputs

Name Type Required Description table table yes The table it read. 
- id: sheet
  plugin: civex.table@1
  config:
    field: sample_sheet     # the file field of this record

- id: save
  plugin: civex.save_records@1
  config:
    schema: Sample
  inputs:
    rows: sheet.table

docs.title: Text files
docs.text: By default (delimiter: auto) the step works out whether a text file separates its columns with commas, tabs or semicolons from the file's own lines (fields inside double quotes are ignored). To fix it, set delimiter to one character or a name (comma, tab, semicolon, pipe, space; \t also means tab), or give delimiters a list the file may use ([comma, tab]): the one that splits every line into the same number of fields wins, then the one that appears most, then the one listed first. A multi-character delimiter is passed to pandas, which reads it as a regular expression. A byte-order mark at the start of a UTF-8 file (common from Excel) is dropped, so it doesn't end up in the first column's name.

docs.title: Excel files
docs.text: The first sheet is read, or the one named in sheet. The file is recognised by its name ending in .xlsx, .xlsm or .xls.

docs.title: civex.value_from_filename@1 (Value from the file name)
docs.text:
Apply a regex to a file field's filename (or a plain string field) and optionally convert the captured value to a typed output. Reach for this when the data you need — a timestamp, a sample number, a session ID — is embedded in a filename rather than stored as its own field. Works with file, file_list, and string fields.

Plugin ID: civex.value_from_filename@1 Category: work-out Capabilities: read

Config

Field Type Required Default Description field string yes The file field whose file name it reads. pattern string no (.+) Regex applied to the filename. The first capture group (or the whole match if there is none) is extracted. output_type string no string Type to convert the captured text to: string | integer | float | date | datetime. date_format string | null no null How the date is written in the name, when it is read as a date, e.g. 'YYYYMMDD-HHmmSS'. Tokens are YYYY MM DD HH mm SS; anything else is a regular expression, so 'YYYYMMDD[-_]HHmmSS' takes a dash or an underscore. Needed for a date or a date and time (output_type date or datetime).

Outputs

Name Type Required Description value any yes The value it took from the name: text, a number or a date. filename string yes The file name it read. extracted string yes The text it took, before it was read as a date or number.

date_format tokens

Token Matches Example YYYY 4-digit year 2024 MM 2-digit month 03 DD 2-digit day 15 HH 2-digit hour (24h) 09 mm 2-digit minute 30 SS 2-digit second 00

All other characters in the format string are treated as raw regex fragments — not strftime codes. This lets you use [-_] to match either a dash or underscore as a separator:

YYYYMMDD[-_]HHmmSS   →  matches  20240315-093000  and  20240315_093000

Extracted datetimes carry no UTC offset: a timestamp in a filename is wall time where the file was made. When the value is saved it is read in the datetime field's timezone restriction, else the collection's timezone, else UTC, and stored as a UTC ISO 8601 string. Set the collection's timezone (civex collection update NAME --timezone Europe/London) so extracted times land on the right instant.

Examples

Extract a datetime from 20240315_093000.csv: 

- id: extract_time
  plugin: civex.value_from_filename@1
  config:
    field: reading
    pattern: '(\d{8}[-_]\d{6})'
    output_type: datetime
    date_format: 'YYYYMMDD[-_]HHmmSS'

Extract a sample number from sample_042_photo.jpg: 

- id: extract_num
  plugin: civex.value_from_filename@1
  config:
    field: photo
    pattern: 'sample_(\d+)'
    output_type: integer
